| When it is sent  | Immediately (in the next write).                                                        | In every update pass, if `x` differs from the last value sent.                        |
| Same value again | Sent again. Use this to pull a control back to the model value after the user moved it. | Not sent. A field the user edited stays as the user left it until your value changes. |
| Write fails      | Retried with back-off (0.25 s doubling up to 30 s).                                     | Not repeated until the value changes.                                                 |
| Typical use      | One-off values: a document, a reset.                                                    | Everything derived from plugin state: labels, enabled flags, lists, status lines.     |

Update passes run after every handler the SDK calls, after player and other state changes, and when you call plugin.update(); several requests are merged into one pass, and each view has at most one write in flight (The update pass has the details).

The rule to remember: **state you change after an `await` inside a handler appears only when the handler finishes**, unless something else triggers a pass. Call `plugin.update()` right after changing it (see Keep a slider responsive while dragging).

##### Two-way controls

A control whose value both the user and the plugin change (a slider, a switch, a text field, a combo box) needs a **two-way binding to an `in-out` property**:

```slint
in-out property <float> strength;
callback strength-changed(float);
Slider {
    value <=> root.strength;                          // two-way: never `value: root.strength`
    changed(value) => { root.strength-changed(value); }
}
```

A one-way binding (`value: root.strength`) is broken by Slint the first time the user moves the control; after that the plugin's writes no longer move it. In a panel or settings page the same applies to the global: `checked <=> MyBridge.enabled`.

#### Theme and widgets

Plugin Slint files import the player's design tokens and widgets:

```slint
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";
import { Icon } from "@vestra/icons.slint";
import { Button, Slider, ToolTipArea, UrlInputRow } from "@vestra/widgets.slint";
import { MarkdownView, MarkdownBlocks, MarkdownBlock } from "@vestra/markdown.slint";
```

- **Colours follow the player's palette.** The player has two palettes, `vestra` (dark, the default) and `vestra-light` (player 0.4.0, SDK 1.5), both drawn from the logo's colours (see plugin.appearance). It sets the palette on every view before it appears and again when the user switches, so `Theme` colours change with it. Colours you hard-code do not. `Theme` properties are read-only.
- **The video area is dark in every palette** (`Theme.bg-video`). Text or icons you draw over the video (a backdrop, an overlay) use light colours, not `Theme.text`, which is dark in `vestra-light`.
- **Use tokens, not values.** `Theme` has colour tokens (`text`, `accent`, `danger` for errors and destructive actions…), font sizes, control sizes and spacing; `Icon { name: "play"; color: Theme.text; }` draws an icon of the player's own set (player 0.4.0, SDK 1.5, so set `"minPlayerVersion": "0.4.0"`); `@vestra/widgets.slint` has the compact `Button`, `Slider`, `ToolTipArea` and `UrlInputRow`. Every token with its current values in both palettes, the icon names and the widgets' properties are in Reference: theme. The values may change between player versions; the tokens keep their meaning.
- **Markdown** (`@vestra/markdown.slint`): `MarkdownView` scrolls one document; `MarkdownBlocks` (SDK 1.5.4, the player after 0.4.0) draws one without scrolling, as tall as its content, for your own layout or a `ListView` row. Both take `blocks: [MarkdownBlock]`, report `link-clicked(url)`, and with `code-copy: true` (default `false`) put a **Copy** button on code blocks (`@tr("Copy")`, which the player translates into the interface language) that reports `copy-code(code)`; copy it with plugin.clipboard. A list of documents (a chat, one message per row) is the example at Ui.markdown; Example: Markdown shows one document in a window.

#### Sizes

All sizes are logical pixels (Slint's `px`): one logical pixel is two physical pixels on a Retina display or at 200 % scaling.

| Surface          | Width                                                                                                                   | Height                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tool window      | The `Window` component's `width` (fixed, not resizable), or `preferred-width` (initial) within `min-width`/`max-width`. | Same with `height`. The title is the component's `title`.                                                                                                      |
| Bottom bar       | The video column's width.                                                                                               | The component's preferred height (within its minimum and maximum). It may draw above its slot into the video area (negative `y`); the player does not clip it. |
| Sidebar          | Set by the user with the splitter (at least 317; the video keeps at least 318).                                         | The window's full height.                                                                                                                                      |
| Floating sidebar | 300 by default, at least 300.                                                                                           | 408 by default, at least 250.                                                                                                                                  |
| Backdrop         | The whole video area.                                                                                                   | The whole video area.                                                                                                                                          |
| Settings page    | 440.                                                                                                                    | The component's height; the Options window scrolls taller pages.                                                                                               |

The operating system places a tool window when it opens; the player does not remember tool window positions or sizes, and the API cannot read or set them. To keep a tool window's _content_ across runs, see Remember a window's state between runs.

#### Focus and keyboard

- **Command key bindings belong to the main window.** A binding from CommandOptions.bindings fires while the main window or the floating sidebar window has focus (and the key was not taken by a focused control, such as Space in a text field). It does **not** fire while a tool window or the Options window has focus. Keys inside your own window are Slint's job: use a `FocusScope` with `key-pressed`, or a button's default action.
- A binding with `focus: "panel"` fires only while this plugin's panel (docked or floating) has focus, and wins over global bindings there.
- **Standard close keys are not bindings.** They close a tool window, the floating sidebar or the Options window like the title-bar button (`onClose` runs) before your Slint handlers or bindings see them; the keys per system are in Keys the system takes first.
- While a menu or a system dialog is open, bindings pause.

#### Platform differences

The API is the same on macOS and Windows; what differs is the system's own part: the standard close keys, how `dialogs.confirm` looks, the monospace font, the modifier `DropModifiers.cmd` stands for. Reference: platforms lists every difference. When the player runs without a user interface (headless, as in some automated setups), opening windows, mounting panels, dialogs, the OSD and `settings.show` fail with `unavailable`.

#### Common pitfalls

- **A window callback bound after the first `show()`.** It throws. Bind all callbacks right after `create()`; re-binding a name that already has a handler is fine.
- **A one-way binding on a control.** `value: root.x` stops following the plugin after the user touches the control. Use `in-out` and `<=>`.
- **`set()` inside a frequent loop.** `set` always sends, even an unchanged value; a periodic `set` of a slider value pulls the thumb back from under the user's pointer. Use `bind` for anything derived from state.
- **Changes after an `await` do not appear.** The update pass runs when the handler finishes; call `plugin.update()` for progress in between.
- **State only inside a panel component.** It is lost when the main window is rebuilt or the sidebar detaches. Keep anything that matters in bridge properties written by the plugin.
- **User edits the plugin does not record.** A settings page or tool window is rebuilt from the plugin's last written values; an `in-out` property the user changed without a callback updating your model reverts. Handle the callback and keep the value in your state (and `bind` it).
- **Hard-coded colours.** They do not follow the palette. Use `Theme.*`, and `Theme.danger` for errors.
- **A `Ctrl+W` default binding.** It never fires in tool windows and floating panels. Pick another key.
- **Two of a kind.** One panel per plugin, one backdrop per player, one OSD info block per plugin, one open dialog at a time (`busy`).
- **An `if` that flips under the pointer.** `if touch.has-hover: Rectangle { … }` (a hover highlight, an accent bar, a tooltip-like box that follows the pointer) creates and destroys an element on every hover change. While a video plays, each such change costs the player's UI thread far more than a property change: the player's accessibility tree (screen readers, UI Automation) is rebuilt for the whole window each time, measured at 100–160 ms per hover on Windows, enough to drop the video to 10–15 frames a second while the pointer moves. Keep the element and change properties instead: `Rectangle { visible: touch.has-hover; … }` or `opacity:`. Use `if` for things that change rarely (a mode, a selection made with a click, a list that was loaded), never for something that follows the pointer or a hover.
- **Slot state without `events`.** PanelSlot.state, appearance.theme and their `onChange` listeners follow other plugins and the user only with the `events` capability.

#### Testing

`TestHost` from `@vestra-player/sdk/testing` runs a plugin without the player and records its interface: windows with their properties and callbacks, the mounted panel, settings pages, the OSD and dialogs. It does not compile Slint files; check them by running the plugin in the player. How to write such tests is in Test a plugin.

## How-to: Control playback

**Goal:** your plugin opens files and controls playback (pause, seek, speed, next and previous), shows what is playing, and never acts on a file the user has already left.

The player has one source. The user, other plugins and yours all change it, so every control in `plugin.player` is **conditional**: it acts on the state your plugin last saw and fails with `stale` (doing nothing) when someone else changed the source in between. Most of this guide is about using that well.

#### Capabilities

```json
{
  "capabilities": ["commands", "playback.read", "playback.control", "events"]
}
```

`playback.read` reads the state, `playback.control` changes it, `events` keeps `player.state` current when the change comes from elsewhere (without it, the state only moves after your own calls and `refresh()`), and `commands` gives your actions menu items and keys.

#### Read the state

`plugin.player.state` is a snapshot the SDK keeps current from the player's events. `onChange` runs after it changed; read the new snapshot there instead of asking the player.

```ts
const info = plugin.osd.panel();
plugin.player.onChange((state) => {
  // `position` and `duration` are seconds, null while unknown.
  if (state.phase !== "ready") return info.set(null);
  info.set("{} / {} s", [state.position?.toFixed(0) ?? "–", state.duration?.toFixed(0) ?? "–"]);
});
```

`state.can` says which controls the current source allows (`pause`, `seek`, `rate`, `restart`, `close`, `next`, `previous`). Bind menu items to it so they grey out by themselves:

```ts
plugin.commands.add({
  id: "pause",
  path: ["@playback", "Pause"],
  enabled: () => plugin.player.state.can.pause, // re-evaluated after every change
  checked: () => plugin.player.state.paused,
  run: () => plugin.player.setPaused(!plugin.player.state.paused),
});
```

#### Control it, and handle `stale`

A control without options is conditional on `player.state` as it is when you call. `stale` means the source changed after that: another file, a close, or any pause, seek or speed change by the user or another plugin. Nothing happened, and usually that is the right outcome:

```ts
try {
  await plugin.player.seek(30);
} catch (error) {
  if ((error as PluginError).code !== "stale") throw error; // another file now
}
```

For work that takes time (a timer, a dialog, a network request), keep the snapshot from when it started and pass it as `ifCurrent`, so the call applies only to that source:

```ts
const seen = plugin.player.state;
const answer = await plugin.dialogs.confirm({ message: "Close this file?", confirm: "Close" }); // ui.dialog
if (answer.confirmed)
  await plugin.player.close({ ifCurrent: seen }).catch((error: PluginError) => {
    if (error.code !== "stale") throw error; // the user opened something else meanwhile
  });
```

`player.isCurrent(seen)` answers the same question without a call. Your own consecutive calls do not make each other stale: the SDK refreshes the state after each one.

Other codes: `invalid` for a value out of range (a negative seek, a speed outside 0.05–10) or a control while nothing is open, `unsupported` for something the source cannot do (a loop on a source that cannot seek).

#### Open a file and follow it

`open` resolves once the player accepted the load (for an address a resolver plugin handles, once the resolver has answered) and returns a `Media` handle for that source. `ready()` waits until it plays; `onEnd` fires when it ends on its own.

```ts
const media = await plugin.player.open("/Movies/clip.mp4");
try {
  await media.ready({ signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) }); // closes it on timeout
} catch (error) {
  await plugin.osd.show("Cannot play: {}", [(error as Error).message]);
}
media.onEnd((ended) =>
  // Play on only if nobody opened something else at the end.
  plugin.player.open("/Movies/next.mp4", { ifCurrent: ended }).catch(() => {}),
);
```

`ready()` rejects with `failed` (the file cannot be loaded), `replaced` (another source took over) or `ended`. Disposing your scope does not close the media: playback belongs to the user, so call `media.close()` when you mean it.

#### Behave exactly like the player's own keys

For buttons in your own bar or window, prefer the player's core actions to calling the controls yourself. `plugin.host.run` (capability `commands`) runs them with the player's checks, accumulation of repeated presses and on-screen text:

```ts
declare const bar: Panel;
// ---cut---
bar.on("playPause", () => plugin.host.run("play-pause"));
bar.on("forward30", () => plugin.host.run("seek-forward", { seconds: 30 })); // adds up with →
```

`run` rejects with `unavailable` while the action is disabled, for example with nothing open.

#### Next and previous

The player's Next and Previous items, keys and buttons ask the **sequence provider**, one plugin at a time, first come first served. The built-in playlist registers as provider when it starts and a built-in plugin cannot be disabled, so in practice another plugin's `provideSequence` is refused (`sequence-taken`); only a development load that replaces the playlist under its id gets it. Any plugin can ask the provider with `player.next()` and `player.previous()`:

```ts
declare const items: string[];
let index = 0;
// ---cut---
const playAt = async (at: number) => {
  index = at;
  await plugin.player.open(items[at]!);
};
plugin.player.provideSequence({
  next: () => playAt(index + 1),
  previous: () => playAt(index - 1),
  canNext: () => index + 1 < items.length, // shown as state.can.next
  canPrevious: () => index > 0,
});
```

A second provider is refused with `conflict` (`sequence-taken`). During activation that does not fail the plugin: it runs without Next and Previous and the player shows a warning; a refusal after activation goes to `onError`.

#### Sliders, loops and the output

- A seek slider: start a `player.scrub()` gesture on press and `end()` it on release; see Keep a slider responsive while dragging.
- An A-B loop: `setLoop({ a, b, count })`; `null` stops it, a new source clears it.
- Volume and mute: `setOutput({ volume, muted })` (volume 0–200). The newest write wins; the promise resolves `false` when a newer one replaced it.
- Your own step size for ← and →: `setStepSeek({ seconds, keyframes })`, withdrawn when your plugin stops.

## How-to: Store a plugin's data

**Goal:** your plugin keeps its settings across restarts, keeps work in progress across a reload, and keeps an API token safe, each in the right place.

| What | Where | Lasts | Capability |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Settings, history, small state | `plugin.storage.json(name)`: a JSON file in the data directory | Across player restarts and plugin upgrades | none |
| Work in progress for this run | `plugin.storage.session`: values in the player's memory | Across plugin restarts (reload, crash, upgrade); cleared when the player quits or the plugin is disabled or uninstalled | none |
| Tokens, passwords | `plugin.secrets`: the system's keychain or Credential Manager | Until deleted, or until the plugin is uninstalled with its data | `secrets` |
| Anything else (caches, downloads) | Your own files under `plugin.dataDirectory` | Until you delete them | none |

All four are private to the plugin; another plugin never reads them.

#### Settings: a JSON file

`storage.json` reads `<dataDirectory>/<name>.json` when you call it and gives you `value` at once (the defaults when the file is missing, broken or fails `validate`; a broken file is kept aside as `<name>.json.bad-<time>`). `save` replaces the value in memory and writes the file 300 ms later, through a temporary file and a rename.

```ts
type Prefs = { step: number; recent: string[] };
const prefs = plugin.storage.json<Prefs>("prefs", {
  defaults: { step: 5, recent: [] },
  // Checked when the file is read: an older version may have written it.
  validate: (v): v is Prefs => typeof (v as Prefs)?.step === "number" && Array.isArray((v as Prefs)?.recent),
});
prefs.save({ ...prefs.value, step: 10 }); // never change prefs.value in place
```

Stopping the plugin writes a pending save first, but only within the short time the player gives a stopping plugin (about 300 ms for a plugin in its own process), and a crash loses it; call `await prefs.flush()` after a save that must not be lost. Also flush before you read or copy the file yourself. See Remember a window's state between runs for a complete window built on a store.

#### Work in progress: session values

`storage.session` keeps JSON values in the player for this run: a reload of the plugin (an upgrade, a crash, the user's Reload) finds them again; the next player start does not.

```ts
const session = plugin.storage.session;
const queue = (await session.get<string[]>("queue")) ?? []; // undefined: nothing stored
queue.push("https://example.com/a.mkv");
try {
  await session.set("queue", queue); // kept once this resolves
} catch (error) {
  // `limit`: the plugin's values would pass 1 MiB; nothing changed.
  if ((error as PluginError).code !== "limit") throw error;
}
```

Each call is one request, answered in order, with no debounce. Keys are 1–1024 bytes; values come back as `JSON.stringify` wrote them (object properties may come back in another order, a `Date` as a string), and are not checked, so check their shape.

#### Secrets: the system's store

`plugin.secrets` stores short text values in the macOS keychain or the Windows Credential Manager. Never write a token to a settings file.

```ts
let token = await plugin.secrets.get("api-token").catch(() => null); // no store: ask
if (token === null) {
  token = "…"; // ask the user, for example in a tool window
  await plugin.secrets.set("api-token", token).catch((error: PluginError) => {
    // `unsupported` (no store), `unavailable` (store unreachable), `failed` (access denied).
    void plugin.osd.show("The token is not kept for next time ({})", [error.code]);
  });
}
```

Names are 1–64 of `a-z 0-9 . _ -`, values 1–1024 bytes, at most 256 names. Have a fallback: some systems have no store, a store can be unreachable (no keychain, read-only, no logged-in session on Windows), and the user can deny access.

#### Your own files

For anything larger (a cache, downloaded files), write under `plugin.dataDirectory` with Node's `fs`. The player deletes the directory only when the plugin is uninstalled together with its data (`packages.uninstall` with `removeData`).

## How-to: Load subtitles from a plugin

**Goal:** your plugin finds subtitles for the playing file (on disk, on a website, by converting another format), adds them as a track, selects them, and optionally styles them.

#### Capabilities

```json
{
  "capabilities": ["subtitles.read", "subtitles.control", "events"]
}
```

`subtitles.read` reads the tracks and the selection; `subtitles.control` changes them (and needs `subtitles.read` too, because every change reads the current selection first); `events` makes the SDK read `plugin.subtitles.state` again when the source or its phase changes. The player has no subtitle event: a selection the user or another plugin changes shows only after `refresh()`.

#### Read the tracks

`plugin.subtitles.state` is `null` until first read; `refresh()` reads it from the player. Each track has an `id` (compare tracks by id), a `kind` (`embedded` in the file or `external`, loaded from a file), a `title` and a `language`.

```ts
const state = plugin.subtitles.state ?? (await plugin.subtitles.refresh());
for (const track of state.tracks)
  console.log(track.id, track.kind, track.language ?? "?", track.title);
// The primary and the secondary subtitle; null when off.
console.log(state.selected?.id, state.secondary?.id);
```

#### Select a track, and handle `stale`

Without options a change reads the newest state itself and applies to it, so it almost never fails. Embedded tracks are chosen by number, though: a `select` after another file opened would pick that file's track with the same number. Pass the state you looked at as `ifCurrent`; then the change fails with `stale`, and does nothing, when the user picked another track or another file opened in between:

```ts
const state = await plugin.subtitles.refresh();
const english = state.tracks.find((track) => track.language === "en");
if (english)
  await plugin.subtitles.select(english, { ifCurrent: state }).catch((error: PluginError) => {
    if (error.code !== "stale") throw error; // the user changed it meanwhile
  });
```

`select(track, { role: "secondary" })` sets the second line shown together with the primary one (a text track other than the primary); `select(null)` turns a role off. A new source clears the secondary subtitle.

#### Upload a file

`load` takes the file's bytes: UTF-8 SRT, or ASS/SSA with `format: "ass"`, at most 2 MiB (SRT up to 10,000 cues, ASS up to 20,000 `Dialogue:` lines). Convert other formats (WebVTT, SAMI) to SRT first. The player adds an `external` track to the current source only, selects it unless `select: "none"`, and resolves with the track once the upload is committed. A plugin has at most 4 such tracks on a source at once and loads at most 16 files into it (removed ones count); past that `load` fails with `busy` (Limits).

```ts
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";
import { basename } from "node:path";
declare const path: string;
// ---cut---
const bytes = await readFile(path);
const track = await plugin.subtitles.load(bytes, {
  format: path.endsWith(".ass") ? "ass" : "srt",
  title: basename(path), // data: shown as it is
  select: "primary",
  signal: AbortSignal.timeout(30_000), // discards the upload if not committed in time
});
await plugin.osd.show("Loaded {}", [track.title]);
```

A title that mixes words with data is a text value the player translates: `title: plugin.i18n.text("{} · {}", [plugin.i18n.text("Downloaded"), name])`. `remove(track)` takes away a track this plugin loaded; the next source removes it anyway.

#### Style the subtitles

`setStyle` sets this plugin's style layer: font (one of `state.fonts`), size at the 1080p reference height, colour, outline, margin, timing offset, box. Each plugin has one layer and its newest call replaces it. When several plugins set a layer, the player shows the one whose **manifest id sorts last**, whatever the order of the calls; `setStyle(null)` takes yours off.

```ts
const { fonts } = await plugin.subtitles.refresh();
if (fonts.length)
  await plugin.subtitles.setStyle({
    fontId: fonts[0]!.id,
    fontSize: 40,
    color: "white",
    outline: 2,
    marginPercent: 5,
    offsetMs: 0, // positive shows them later
  });
```

## How-to: Keep a slider responsive while dragging

**Goal:** a slider in your window drives something live (a video filter, the volume, a preview), the effect follows the pointer while the user drags, and nothing lags behind or queues up.

A slider reports every pointer movement, often more than 60 times a second. Each report is a callback in your plugin. The plugin stays responsive if every callback only **records the newest value and hands it to something that keeps only the newest value**. It stutters when every callback starts its own slow request and the requests queue up behind each other.

#### The complete example

A **Brightness** window with a slider from −1 to 1, a value label and a Reset button. The video follows the slider while it moves; an on-screen message reports the value when the user lets go.

`manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "examples.brightness",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.3.0",
  "capabilities": [
    "commands",
    "ui.window",
    "ui.osd",
    "processing.video",
    "playback.read",
    "events"
  ]
}
```

`ui/brightness.slint`:

```slint
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";
import { Button, Slider } from "@vestra/widgets.slint";

export component BrightnessWindow inherits Window {
    title: "Brightness";
    width: 300px;
    background: Theme.bg-panel;

    // Written by the plugin and by the slider: in-out, bound two-way below.
    in-out property <float> brightness;
    in property <string> label;
    callback brightness-changed(float); // every pointer move
    callback brightness-released(float); // once, when the button is released
    callback reset();

    HorizontalLayout {
        padding: Theme.dialog-padding;
        spacing: 8px;
        Slider {
            minimum: -1;
            maximum: 1;
            value <=> root.brightness;
            changed(value) => { root.brightness-changed(value); }
            released(value) => { root.brightness-released(value); }
        }
        Text {
            width: 36px;
            text: root.label;
            color: Theme.text;
            font-size: Theme.font-body;
            horizontal-alignment: right;
            vertical-alignment: center;
        }
        Button {
            text: "Reset";
            small: true;
            clicked => { root.reset(); }
        }
    }
}
```

`main.ts`:

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  let brightness = 0; // the model: −1–1, 0 = unchanged

  // A filter keeps one request in flight and sends only the newest value.
  const filter = plugin.video.filter("brightness");
  const apply = () =>
    filter.set([
      { kind: "eq", brightness, contrast: 1, saturation: 1, gamma: 1 },
    ]);

  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/brightness.slint");
  // Derived from the model: sent only when it changes.
  window.bind(() => ({ brightness, label: brightness.toFixed(2) }));

  window.on("brightnessChanged", (value: number) => {
    brightness = Math.min(1, Math.max(-1, value)); // record the newest value…
    apply(); // …and hand it on; no await
  });
  window.on("brightnessReleased", () => {
    void plugin.osd.show(`Brightness ${brightness.toFixed(2)}`); // once per drag
  });
  window.on("reset", () => {
    brightness = 0; // the bound value moves the slider back
    apply();
  });

  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "brightness",
    path: ["@video", "Brightness…"],
    run: () => window.show(),
  });
}
```

#### Why this stays smooth

1. **The callback does not wait.** `brightnessChanged` updates a variable and calls `filter.set()`, which returns at once. The SDK runs the next callback as soon as it arrives.
2. **The expensive part keeps only the newest value.** `filter.set()` has _latest-value_ semantics: while one request is in flight, newer values replace each other and only the last one is sent. A fast drag costs a request per round trip to the player, not one per pointer move, and the video ends exactly where the slider stopped.
3. **The slider's value is bound, not set.** `bind` sends `brightness` only when it differs from what was sent last, and the player skips a write that equals what the slider already shows. So the plugin never fights the user's pointer, yet Reset (which changes the model) moves the thumb.
4. **Work that should happen once happens on release.** The on-screen message (and anything like saving or logging) waits for `brightnessReleased`, which fires once per drag.

The Slint side needs two things: an `in-out` property and a two-way binding (`value <=> root.brightness`). With a one-way binding (`value: root.brightness`) Slint breaks the binding the first time the user drags, and Reset stops moving the thumb.

#### Which calls keep only the newest value

| Latest value wins (safe on every move)                                                                                 | One request per call (do not call on every move)                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| VideoFilter`.set`, AudioFilter`.set` | player.seek: use player.scrub() and `Scrub.seek` for a seek slider |
| player.setOutput (volume, mute)                                          | `player.setRate` and other player controls                                                                                                            |
| `Scrub.seek` (about one seek per display frame)                                                                        | osd.show: show a message on release                                                                             |
| View properties (`bind`, `set`), OsdPanel.set                                | `JsonStore.save` is debounced (300 ms), so it is fine; anything you write yourself is not                                                             |

#### When the slow part is your own code

If a move triggers your own asynchronous work (rendering a preview with `plugin.tools.run`, a network request), do not `await` it per callback: the SDK starts every callback without waiting for the previous one, so slow runs overlap and can finish out of order, leaving an _older_ result on screen. Give that work latest-value semantics yourself:

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

/** Run `work` for the newest value only: one run at a time; values that arrive meanwhile replace each other. */
export function latest<T>(work: (value: T) => Promise<void>) {
  let running = false;
  let next: { value: T } | undefined;
  return async (value: T) => {
    next = { value };
    if (running) return; // the running loop picks it up
    running = true;
    try {
      while (next) {
        const current = next.value;
        next = undefined;
        await work(current);
      }
    } finally {
      running = false;
    }
  };
}

declare function renderPreview(strength: number): Promise<string>; // your own slow work

export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  let preview = "";
  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/preview.slint");
  window.bind(() => ({ preview }));
  const refresh = latest(async (strength: number) => {
    preview = await renderPreview(strength);
    plugin.update(); // changed after an await: send it now
  });
  window.on("strengthChanged", (strength: number) => refresh(strength));
}
```

`plugin.update()` matters here. The SDK re-evaluates bound properties after a callback returns and again when its promise settles; a value you change **after an `await`** inside a longer task is otherwise shown only when that task ends. Call `plugin.update()` whenever such a task has something new to show.

## How-to: Remember a window's state between runs

**Goal:** a tool window comes back the way the user left it: its controls hold the last values, and if it was open when the player quit, it opens again at the next start.

A tool window keeps nothing by itself: closing it destroys the window instance, and the plugin process ends with the player. Keep the state in your plugin, store it with plugin.storage.json, show it with `bind`, and reopen the window during activation.

#### The complete example

The **Brightness** window from Keep a slider responsive while dragging, now remembering the brightness and whether the window was open. The manifest is the same as there, without `ui.osd`:

```json
{
  "id": "examples.brightness",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.3.0",
  "capabilities": [
    "commands",
    "ui.window",
    "processing.video",
    "playback.read",
    "events"
  ]
}
```

`ui/brightness.slint` is unchanged: it declares `in-out property <float> brightness`, `in property <string> label` and the callbacks `brightness-changed(float)`, `brightness-released(float)` and `reset()` (the full file is on the slider page).

`main.ts`:

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

/** Everything the plugin remembers, in <dataDirectory>/brightness.json. */
interface Saved {
  /** −1–1, 0 = unchanged. */
  brightness: number;
  /** The window was open when the player quit. */
  open: boolean;
}

const DEFAULTS: Saved = { brightness: 0, open: false };

/** A missing, broken or outdated file falls back to DEFAULTS. */
function isSaved(value: unknown): value is Saved {
  const v = value as Partial<Saved> | null;
  return (
    typeof v === "object" &&
    v !== null &&
    typeof v.brightness === "number" &&
    Math.abs(v.brightness) <= 1 &&
    typeof v.open === "boolean"
  );
}

export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  // 1. Load: read once, synchronously; defaults if there is no valid file.
  const store = plugin.storage.json<Saved>("brightness", {
    defaults: DEFAULTS,
    validate: isSaved,
  });
  /** Change part of the state; the file is written 300 ms after the last change. */
  const remember = (patch: Partial<Saved>) =>
    store.save({ ...store.value, ...patch });

  const filter = plugin.video.filter("brightness");
  const apply = () =>
    filter.set([
      {
        kind: "eq",
        brightness: store.value.brightness,
        contrast: 1,
        saturation: 1,
        gamma: 1,
      },
    ]);
  apply(); // the effect is back before the window is

  // 2. Show: the window always displays the stored state.
  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/brightness.slint");
  window.bind(() => ({
    brightness: store.value.brightness,
    label: store.value.brightness.toFixed(2),
  }));
  window.on("brightnessChanged", (value: number) => {
    remember({ brightness: Math.min(1, Math.max(-1, value)) });
    apply();
  });
  window.on("reset", () => {
    remember({ brightness: 0 });
    apply();
  });

  // 3. Track whether it is open: only the user closing it counts as "closed".
  window.onClose(() => remember({ open: false }));
  const open = async () => {
    await window.show();
    remember({ open: true });
  };
  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "brightness",
    path: ["@video", "Brightness…"],
    run: open,
  });

  // 4. Restore: reopen it if it was open when the player quit.
  if (store.value.open) await open().catch(() => remember({ open: false }));
}
```

#### How it works

- **Load once, at activation.** `storage.json` reads `<dataDirectory>/brightness.json` synchronously when it is created. A file that cannot be parsed or fails `validate` is renamed to `brightness.json.bad-<timestamp>` and `defaults` is used, so a damaged or older file never breaks the plugin. Always pass a `validate` function: the file is outside your control.
- **Bind the stored value, not a copy.** `window.bind` reads `store.value` in every update pass, so whatever changes the state (a callback, Reset, a command) updates the window, and a window opened later starts with the current values.
- **Save on every change; the store debounces.** `save()` replaces `store.value` at once and writes the file 300 ms after the last call (a temporary file, then a rename). Dragging the slider writes the file once, after the drag. When the plugin stops (the player quits, the user disables the plugin), the store is flushed, so the last value is not lost.
- **"Open" means "the user did not close it".** `onClose` runs only when the user closes the window (the title-bar button or the standard close keys). When the player quits, the plugin stops and its windows close _without_ `onClose`, so `open` stays `true` and the window comes back next time. That is the behaviour users expect from an application's tool windows.
- **Restore after binding.** The window is created and bound before `open()` runs, so it opens with the stored values and without flashing defaults. If it cannot open (for example in a player without a user interface), the plugin forgets that it was open instead of failing activation.

#### What you cannot restore

- **Position and size.** The operating system places a tool window when it opens. The player does not remember tool window frames, and the API has no way to read or set them; the window's size comes from its Slint file (`width`, `preferred-width` and so on).
- **State that only Slint knows.** Text in a field, a scroll position or a selected tab survives only if a callback reports it to the plugin and the plugin stores it and writes it back as a property, as `brightness` does here.

#### Variations

- **Several windows from one file** (one per document, created with `windows.create(file, { id })`): store an object keyed by the window id and restore each one.
- **Preferences rather than state:** a choice such as "reopen my windows at startup" belongs on a settings page (plugin.settings.page) that reads and writes the same store (the `SettingsPage` reference has an example).
- **Large or binary data:** write your own files in plugin.dataDirectory (to a temporary name, then rename) and keep only small settings in `storage.json`.

## How-to: Offer a GPU rendering switch

**Goal:** a settings menu item "GPU Rendering (Experimental)" that shows whether the player will draw on the GPU, is greyed out with the player's reason where the GPU cannot be chosen, saves the user's choice, says "(Restart to Apply)" while the choice waits for a restart, and offers that restart.

The player keeps the choice itself, like a browser's hardware acceleration switch: setPreference saves it in the player's settings at once, the running player keeps its renderer, and the next start uses the choice **whether or not the user restarts now**. Your plugin stores nothing. Reading the state needs no capability; saving a choice and restarting need `rendering.manage`, which needs player 0.5.13.

#### The complete example

`manifest.json`:

```json
{
  "id": "examples.gpu-switch",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.5.13",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "rendering.manage"]
}
```

`main.ts`:

```ts
import type { Plugin, PluginError, RenderingState, Scope } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

const TITLE = "GPU Rendering (Experimental)";

export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  let state: RenderingState = await plugin.rendering.state();
  let menu: Scope | null = null;
  let shownPending: boolean | null = null;

  // A command's title cannot change in place, so the items live in a child
  // scope that is rebuilt when `restartPending` flips.
  async function build() {
    if (state.restartPending === shownPending) return;
    shownPending = state.restartPending;
    await menu?.dispose();
    menu = plugin.scope();
    menu.commands.add({
      id: "gpu-rendering",
      path: ["@settings", state.restartPending ? `${TITLE} (Restart to Apply)` : TITLE],
      // Checked when the next start draws on the GPU (also for "auto").
      checked: () => state.nextMode === "gpu",
      // Greyed out with the player's reason where "gpu" cannot be chosen.
      enabled: () => state.gpu.available,
      reason: () => state.gpu.reason?.message ?? null,
      run: async () => {
        const choice = state.nextMode === "gpu" ? "software" : "gpu";
        try {
          state = await plugin.rendering.setPreference(choice);
        } catch (error) {
          // `unavailable`: the GPU was ruled out after the state was read.
          state = await plugin.rendering.state(); // the item now says why
          if ((error as PluginError).code !== "unavailable") throw error; // `failed`: not saved
        } finally {
          await build();
        }
      },
    });
    if (state.restartPending)
      menu.commands.add({
        id: "restart",
        path: ["@settings", "Restart Player to Apply"],
        run: async () => {
          // Resolves once the player accepted; it then quits and starts again.
          await plugin.rendering.restartPlayer();
        },
      });
  }

  await build();
}
```

#### How it works

- **`state()` describes now and the next start.** `mode` and `reason` are the renderer drawing now and why; `preference` is the saved choice (`"auto"`, `"gpu"` or `"software"`); `nextMode` and `nextReason` are what the next start will use as far as the player knows, after the environment, the driver denylist and an earlier GPU crash. The item is checked by `nextMode`, so with `"auto"` on a system where the GPU is the default it shows checked.
- **`gpu.available` decides whether the item can be used.** Where this player has no GPU renderer (`no-gpu-backend`, Windows today), without a user interface (`headless`), for a graphics driver on the player's denylist (`denylist`) or after a GPU crash at an earlier start (`previous-crash`), it is `false` and `gpu.reason.message` explains why; the item shows that as its disabled reason. `"software"` and `"auto"` are always accepted, so a user can always leave the GPU.
- **`restartPending`** is true while the next start's mode differs from the mode this run started with. When the user changes the choice back, it turns false again and the "(Restart to Apply)" title and the restart item go away.
- **`restartPlayer()`** resolves once the player has accepted. The player then quits normally, which stops every plugin, yours included, and starts again with the same plugins; a local file continues at its position, paused or playing as it was (a stream is not reopened). It rejects with `busy` while a restart is under way and with `failed` when the new process could not start (the player keeps running).

The restart is only a shortcut. A user who ignores it gets the new renderer the next time they start the player.

#### Older players

A player before 0.5.13 does not load a plugin that declares `rendering.manage`, so the manifest above sets `minPlayerVersion`. A plugin that only reads the state, without the capability, gets `unsupported` from `state()` on an older player:

```ts
const state = await plugin.rendering.state().catch((error: PluginError) => {
  if (error.code === "unsupported") return null; // a player before 0.5.13
  throw error;
});
```

To know only whether render options work now, read rendering from `plugin.app.system()` instead; `renderingReason` there is the same reason as `state().reason`.

#### Test it

TestHost.rendering models the player: preset `gpu`, `reason` and `startedWith` before the plugin starts (`videoRender.gpu` is the mode drawing now), then drive the item and check the saved choice.

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { startPlugin, TestHost } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

const host = new TestHost(); // a GPU player, "auto", started on the GPU
const { stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
  directory: new URL("..", import.meta.url),
  host,
});
await host.command("gpu-rendering").run(); // unchecks: saves "software"
assert.equal(host.rendering.preference, "software");
await host.command("restart").run(); // offered while the restart is pending
assert.equal(host.rendering.restarts, 1);
await stop();
```

Set `host.rendering.gpu = { available: false, reason: { code: "denylist", message: "…" } }` to see the item greyed out, and refuse a call with `host.handle("rendering.restart", () => { throw new HostError("failed", "…"); })`.

## How-to: Translate a plugin

Vestra Player (0.4.3 or later) shows its interface in one of seven languages. The user picks one in **Settings ▸ Language** (or follows the system); the choice takes effect at the next start, and the language stays the same for the whole run. A plugin joins in by shipping one gettext file per language. It writes **no translation code**: the player translates.

The Counter example is a complete translated plugin. Moving an existing plugin over is in Migrate a plugin to English source text.

#### The rule: English source text in three places

Every text a user can see is written in English, in one of three places, and the player looks it up in the plugin's catalog for the interface language. Untranslated text shows in English.

1. **Declarations.** What the plugin declares, the player shows translated:

   ```ts nocheck
   plugin.commands.add({
     id: "counter",
     path: ["Tools", "Counter…"], // English: menus merge by these words
     run: () => window.show(),
   });
   ```

   Command titles and paths, settings page titles (`settings.page`), panel and tab titles (`panels.mount`), command `reason`s, and the manifest's `name`, `punchline`, `description` and `tags`. Menus of different plugins merge by the English words, so plugins that share a submenu must write it the same way; the player's own menus are `Open`, `Playback`, `Subtitles`, `Video`, `Audio`, `Screen`, `Settings` (or `@video` and the other ids) and show in the player's words.

2. **Slint.** A window's texts belong in its `.slint` file, wrapped in `@tr`:

   ```slint
   title: @tr("Counter");
   Text { text: @tr("{n} click" | "{n} clicks" % root.count); }
   Button { text: @tr("Add {}", root.step); }
   ```

   TypeScript passes data (`count`, `step`), never finished sentences. `@tr` takes `{}`, `{0}`, `{1}` arguments and a plural form (`"one" | "other" % n`, where `{n}` is the number). The player has two plural forms: one for `n == 1`, the other for every other number. A context (`@tr("Menu" => "Open")`) tells two meanings of one English word apart.

3. **Sentences the plugin hands the player**: `osd.show`, `OsdPanel.set` and `dialogs.confirm` take a template and its arguments:

   ```ts nocheck
   await plugin.osd.show("Speed {}×", [rate]);
   await plugin.dialogs.confirm({
     message: "Delete {} bookmarks?",
     confirm: "Delete",
     args: [count],
   });
   ```

   Never build the sentence in TypeScript (`` `Speed ${rate}×` ``, `"Speed " + rate`): a translator can only translate a whole template, and word order differs between languages. Named arguments work too: `osd.show("{name} is ready", { name })`.

`plugin.i18n.locale` tells which language this run uses, for what is not text (a date: `date.toLocaleDateString(plugin.i18n.locale)`). There is no `t()` function and no event when the language changes: it never changes while the player runs.

#### Text that mixes words and data

Some text is neither a fixed declaration nor a window Slint can build: a menu item "Track 2 (opus)", a ComboBox model whose first item is "No Audio" and the rest track names, an OSD message whose reason is itself a sentence, a list of file names. For these, make a **text value** with `plugin.i18n.text(source, args)` (SDK 1.5.11, player 0.4.3) and pass it where a string would go. It is plain data, not a translation: the player translates `source` with the plugin's catalog and fills in the arguments when it shows it.

```ts nocheck
const { text, list } = plugin.i18n;

// A menu item with data (the menu merges by the English "Track 2 (opus)").
plugin.commands.add({
  id: `track-${n}`,
  path: ["@audio", "Audio Track", text("Track {} ({})", [n, codec])],
  run,
});

// A [string] model: fixed words and data in one list.
picker.set({ labels: [text("No Audio"), ...tracks.map((t) => text("Track {} · {}", [t.id, t.title]))] });

// An argument that is a sentence of its own.
await plugin.osd.show("Download failed: {}", [text("Connection timed out")]);

// Items joined the language's way: "a.glsl, b.glsl", "a.glsl、b.glsl".
await plugin.osd.show("Removed missing shaders: {}", [list(missing)]);

// A message of several parts, each translated: "Added: 3, duplicates skipped: 2".
await plugin.osd.show(list([text("Added: {}", [added]), text("duplicates skipped: {}", [skipped])], "clauses"));
```

Arguments are data (strings and numbers, shown as they are) unless they are text values themselves, which are translated too, to any depth (8 levels). `list(items, style)` joins with the interface language's separator: `"list"` (`, ` / `、`), `"clauses"` (`, ` / `，`), `"semicolons"`, `"sentences"` (`. ` / `。`) or `"lines"`.

A text value is accepted wherever the player shows a plugin's text:

| Where | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `commands.add` `title`, `path` segments, `reason`; `Command.set({ reason })` | not a `list`; the menu merges by the English rendering |
| `osd.show(value)`, `OsdPanel.set(value)`, and as their `args` | a text value as the message carries its own args |
| `dialogs.confirm` `message`, `detail`, `confirm`, `cancel`, `checkbox` | `args` fills only the string ones |
| file dialog `title`; `saveFile` `fileName` | a string `fileName` is data; `text("Playlist.m3u8")` is translated |
| window, panel and settings page properties, where Slint has `string` | at any depth: `[string]` models, struct fields |
| `TimelineLayer.set` mark titles, `subtitles.load({ title })` | a plain string stays data |
| a resolver's failure: `throw plugin.i18n.error("The ROM file was not found.")` | shown translated as the open's failure and `player.state.error` |

`extract` collects the `source` of every `text(…)` and `error(…)` call (literals, `?:` branches, `as const` tables), whether called as `plugin.i18n.text` or destructured. Write the source as a literal, never `` text(`Track ${n}`) ``. A source made only of placeholders and punctuation (`"{} ({})"`, `"{0}: {1}"`) is collected like any other: languages differ in punctuation too (Chinese writes `"{}（{}）"`, `"{0}：{1}"`), and a translator who keeps it as it is simply copies it.

**Text that leaves the player.** What the plugin copies to the clipboard or writes to a file is not shown by the player. For that only, `plugin.i18n.resolve(value)` returns the translated string (with the same catalog the player uses): `clipboard.writeText(resolve(list(lines, "lines")))`. Never use it for the interface: a string resolved in TypeScript and then shown would hide the sentence from `check`, and the interface takes text values directly.

**OSD panel lines that must fit.** `OsdPanel.set(value, args, { maxColumns })` cuts each line after translation (a Chinese, Japanese or Korean character is two columns), so the plugin does not measure translated text.

#### Languages

The player's interface languages, and the locale code that names a language's catalog file and is `plugin.i18n.locale` in a run:

| Code | Language | Shown in the menu as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `en` | English (source language) | English |
| `zh-Hans` | Simplified Chinese | 简体中文 |
| `ja` | Japanese | 日本語 |
| `ko` | Korean | 한국어 |
| `de` | German | Deutsch |
| `fr` | French | Français |
| `es` | Spanish | Español |

A plugin may ship any subset; a `.po` file named after a code not in this table is reported by `i18n check` and never read by the player.

#### Files

```text
locales/
  messages.pot     every text to translate (written by vestra-plugin i18n extract)
  zh-Hans.po       Simplified Chinese
  de.po            German …
```

One `<lang>.po` per language you provide, named by its locale (the codes in Languages; English is the source and has none). They are ordinary gettext files: any `.po` editor (Poedit, Lokalize, Weblate, a text editor) works. `vestra-plugin build` compiles them into `dist/locales/<lang>.json`, which the player reads; during development (`--plugin <dir>`) the player reads the `.po` files directly.

#### Commands

```sh
vestra-plugin i18n extract                # write locales/messages.pot, update every locales/<lang>.po
vestra-plugin i18n extract --locale de    # start a new language
vestra-plugin i18n check                  # coverage and problems; fails on stale catalogs
```

`extract` finds every `@tr` in the `.slint` files, the texts given to the calls above (literals, both branches of a `?:`, and `as const` tables, through the TypeScript type checker), and the manifest's display fields. It keeps existing translations, adds new texts untranslated, and moves texts that disappeared to the end of each `.po` as obsolete (`#~`), so a text that comes back keeps its translation. Comments you write yourself stay where they are (SDK 1.5.13): lines before the header (`# Reviewed by … on 2026-10-25`, `# Translator: …`) and `# ` comments on an entry. A plural entry gets exactly as many `msgstr[n]` lines as the file's `Plural-Forms` has `nplurals`: one for Japanese, Korean and Simplified Chinese (an empty `msgstr[1]` left from an older SDK is removed), two for the others.

`check` reports per language how much is translated, translations that lost or changed a placeholder (keep every `{…}` exactly as in the English; reorder with `{0}`, `{1}` only where the English has them), plural forms missing, a stale `messages.pot`, and text that cannot be translated: a sentence composed in TypeScript, a value that is not a literal, Chinese or other non-English source text, and Slint text without `@tr`. These are warnings, except that `i18n check` fails (exit code 1, SDK 1.5.12) when `messages.pot` is out of date or a `.po` lacks some of its messages: run `extract` and commit the result, so CI catches a forgotten `extract`. `vestra-plugin check` prints the same lines when the plugin has a `locales/` folder; none of them fails `check` or a build.

A note for translators goes in a comment that starts with `TRANSLATORS:` right before the text (in TypeScript on the property or the call, or on an entry of an `as const` table (SDK 1.5.12); in Slint on the line above the `@tr`); `extract` copies it into the files.

```ts nocheck
const REASONS = {
  // TRANSLATORS: the download took longer than 30 seconds.
  timeout: "Connection timed out",
  dns: "Server not found",
} as const;
```

#### Machine translations and review

A translation made by a machine (or a language model) is marked as such until a person who knows the language has checked it, so that a reader of the file can tell which entries nobody has looked at yet.

- **Flag each machine-translated entry `x-machine`**, in the entry's `#,` line before its `msgid` (next to `fuzzy`, separated by a comma: `#, fuzzy, x-machine`):

  ```po
  #. The button that adds one to the count.
  #: ui/counter.slint:12
  #, x-machine
  msgid "Add {}"
  msgstr "{} hinzufügen"
  ```

  The flag is only for people. The player and the SDK read `fuzzy` alone (a fuzzy entry is left out of the catalog) and ignore every other flag, so an `x-machine` entry is compiled and shown like any other. `i18n extract` keeps the flag with the translation, also when the text becomes obsolete (`#~`).
- **A review of the whole file goes in a header comment**: a line before the `msgid ""` header, such as `# Reviewed by an AI reviewer on 2026-10-25` or `# Reviewed by Jane Doe on 2026-10-25 (menus and settings)`. `extract` keeps lines before the header (SDK 1.5.13). An automatic review does not replace a human one: it leaves the `x-machine` flags in place.
- **A human reviewer removes the flag.** Someone who knows the language reads each entry, corrects what is wrong and then deletes that entry's `x-machine` (from `#, fuzzy, x-machine` only `x-machine`; remove the `#,` line when nothing is left). An entry still flagged has not been reviewed: `grep -c x-machine locales/de.po` counts what is left. When the whole file is done, the header comment names the reviewer and the date.

Translations written by a person from the start carry no flag.

#### Tests

`startPlugin(activate, { directory, locale: "zh-Hans" })` loads `locales/zh-Hans.po` and makes the test host show what a user of that language sees:

```ts nocheck
const { host, plugin, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, { directory, locale: "zh-Hans" });
assert.equal(plugin.i18n.locale, "zh-Hans");
assert.deepEqual(host.command("counter").display.path, ["工具", "计数器…"]);
assert.deepEqual(host.osd, ["计数：1"]); // osd.show("Count: {}", [1])
```

`command.display` is the menu as shown (`display.reason` the shown reason), `host.osd`, `host.osdPanel` and `host.confirmTexts` the shown messages, `host.fileDialogs` the file dialogs' titles and file names, window and panel `props` the property values with their text values shown, `host.translate(text, args)` any text (a string or a text value). The declared English stays in `command.declaration` and `host.sent(...)`. Without `locale`, the plugin's own texts show in English as declared, but the player's own texts (core action OSD messages, menu titles and reasons) stay in Simplified Chinese, as in SDK 1.5.8 and older, so existing tests keep passing; pass `locale: "en"` to see the player in English.

#### Limits

- The language changes only at the next start of the player.
- Plurals have two forms (1 and everything else). For a language with more forms (Russian, Arabic, Polish) the player does not ship a translation.
- Numbers in templates print as JavaScript writes them (`1.5`), not in the language's own format.
- A text the player cannot find in the catalog shows in English; so does a plugin's text on a player before 0.4.3, which also shows templates without filling them in. Set `"minPlayerVersion": "0.4.3"` in the manifest of a plugin that relies on templates or text values (older players run an older SDK, which has no `plugin.i18n.text`).
- Text values have limits on arguments, list items, nesting and bytes (Text values); a property value's limits (Property values) count a text value as the string it becomes.

## How-to: Migrate a plugin to English source text

For plugins written before SDK 1.5.9 whose texts are in one language (Chinese, for the plugins built into Vestra Player). After the migration every text is English in the source, and the old texts become the first translation. The behaviour stays the same: a user with the same language sees exactly the texts as before. Read Translate a plugin first; this page is the checklist.

Needs player 0.4.3 or later: set `"minPlayerVersion": "0.4.3"` in `manifest.json`.

#### 1. Menus: English paths

Before:

```ts nocheck
plugin.commands.add({ id: "snapshot", path: ["视频", "截图", "保存当前画面…"], run: save });
```

After:

```ts nocheck
plugin.commands.add({ id: "snapshot", path: ["@video", "Snapshot", "Save Current Frame…"], run: save });
```

- The player's menus: `@open`, `@playback`, `@subtitles`, `@video`, `@audio`, `@screen`, `@settings` (or their keys `Open`, `Playback`, `Subtitles`, `Video`, `Audio`, `Screen`, `Settings`). Its own submenus `Playback ▸ Speed` and `Playback ▸ Seek` keep the player's words too. The old Chinese titles of these menus (视频, 播放 ▸ 速度 …) still work, so an unmigrated plugin lands in the same menus meanwhile.
- **Shared submenus merge by the English words.** When another plugin puts items into the same submenu, both must write it identically. Submenu keys in use lists the English keys the player and its built-in plugins use; reuse those, and ask before inventing a new shared one.
- Title case for menu items ("Save Current Frame…"), an ellipsis `…` when the item opens a window or asks something.
- Dynamic items (tracks, devices, presets) whose titles are data (a file name, a device name) stay data: they are not translated. Items whose titles come from a fixed list are text: put the list in an `as const` table so `extract` finds them:

  ```ts nocheck
  const RATES = [
    { id: "half", title: "0.5×" },
    { id: "double", title: "2×" },
  ] as const;
  ```

- `order`, `group`, `radio`, `bindings` do not change. Saved user key bindings are kept: they are stored by plugin and command id, not by path.

#### 2. Slint: `@tr`

Before:

```slint
Button { text: "恢复默认"; }
Text { text: root.count + " 个文件"; }
```

After:

```slint
Button { text: @tr("Restore Defaults"); }
Text { text: @tr("{n} file" | "{n} files" % root.count); }
```

Wrap every literal a user reads (`text`, `title`, `placeholder-text`, `tip`, default values of properties shown as text). Do not concatenate in Slint either: `"[" + a + "]"` becomes `@tr("[{}]", a)`.

#### 3. Sentences built in TypeScript

The plugin may no longer build a user-visible sentence in TypeScript. Three ways out, in this order of preference:

**Into the Slint file.** When a window shows it, let the window build it from data:

```ts nocheck
// Before: TypeScript composes the tooltip.
panel.bind(() => ({ tipBack: `后退 ${step} 秒 (${key})` }));
// After: TypeScript passes data; Slint has text: @tr("Back {} s ({})", root.step, root.key)
panel.bind(() => ({ step, key }));
```

**A template with arguments**, for the OSD and dialogs:

```ts nocheck
// Before
plugin.osd.show(`播放速度：${rate}x`);
plugin.dialogs.confirm({ message: `删除 ${n} 个书签？`, confirm: "删除" });
// After
plugin.osd.show("Speed: {}x", [rate]);
plugin.dialogs.confirm({ message: "Delete {} bookmarks?", confirm: "Delete", args: [n] });
```

Arguments are data and are not translated. When an argument would itself be a word from a fixed set (a palette name, "on"/"off"), write one whole template per value instead, so each is translated as a sentence:

```ts nocheck
// Before
plugin.osd.show(`配色：${theme === "vestra" ? "Vestra 深色" : "Vestra 浅色"}`);
// After: both branches are found by extract
plugin.osd.show(theme === "vestra" ? "Palette: Vestra Dark" : "Palette: Vestra Light");
```

**A text value** (SDK 1.5.11), when the words and the data cannot be separated into a Slint file or one template: a menu item with a number, a `[string]` model, a sentence made of translated parts, a list.

```ts nocheck
const { text, list } = plugin.i18n;
// Before: the old Chinese, or English that a Chinese user then saw
plugin.commands.add({ id, path: ["@audio", "Audio Track", `Track ${n} (${codec})`], run });
tune.bind(() => ({ trackLabels: ["关闭字幕", ...names] }));
plugin.osd.show("Download failed: {}", [english(reason)]);
plugin.osd.show("Removed missing shaders: {}", [missing.join("、")]);
// After
plugin.commands.add({ id, path: ["@audio", "Audio Track", text("Track {} ({})", [n, codec])], run });
tune.bind(() => ({ trackLabels: [text("Subtitles Off"), ...names] }));
plugin.osd.show("Download failed: {}", [text(REASONS[reason])]);
plugin.osd.show("Removed missing shaders: {}", [list(missing)]);
```

The table of where text values are accepted is in Translate a plugin. A resolver's failure: `throw plugin.i18n.error("The ROM file was not found.")`. Text for the clipboard or a file: `plugin.i18n.resolve(value)`, never for the interface.

**Status texts as data.** A text that a window shows depending on state (`"正在载入…"`, `"没有音轨"`) becomes a state value (`loading: true`) that the Slint file turns into words.

Error messages that come from the player or the SDK (`error.message`) are not the plugin's text: showing them as they are is fine, but do not put them into a template of your own.

#### 4. The manifest

`name`, `punchline`, `description` and `tags` are English; their translations go in the same `.po` files (`extract` collects them). The plugin manager and the store show them translated (`PluginInfo.display`).

#### 5. Write `zh-Hans.po` from the old text

```sh
vestra-plugin i18n extract --locale zh-Hans   # locales/messages.pot and an empty locales/zh-Hans.po
```

Then fill every `msgstr` with the text the plugin showed before. That text **is** the translation; copy it exactly, including punctuation and spacing, so users see no change. Placeholders stay as in the English: `msgid "Speed: {}x"` → `msgstr "播放速度：{}x"`. A plural entry in Simplified Chinese needs only `msgstr[0]`. A `git diff` of the migration shows each old text next to its new English.

#### 6. Check

```sh
vestra-plugin i18n extract    # again after every source change
vestra-plugin i18n check      # until it prints nothing but the coverage line
```

`check` finds what is left: Chinese text in TypeScript or Slint, Slint text without `@tr`, sentences composed in TypeScript, values it cannot read, translations whose placeholders differ.

#### 7. Tests

- Assertions on declarations now see English: `command.declaration.path` is what the code declared.
- To check what a Chinese user sees, start with `locale: "zh-Hans"` and assert on `command.display`, `host.osd`, `host.confirmTexts`; the old expected strings usually stay as they were.
- `startPlugin` without `locale` plays English for the plugin's texts but keeps the player's own messages (core actions, refusals) in Chinese, as before 1.5.9. Pass `locale` to get the player's English.

```ts nocheck
const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, { directory, locale: "zh-Hans" });
assert.deepEqual(host.command("snapshot").display.path, ["视频", "截图", "保存当前画面…"]);
```

#### Before you hand it in

- [ ] No user-visible Chinese (or other non-English) text left in `.ts` and `.slint` files.
- [ ] Every Slint text in `@tr`; no sentence composed in TypeScript.
- [ ] `locales/messages.pot` up to date, `locales/zh-Hans.po` complete (`check`: `zh-Hans: N/N translated`).
- [ ] Shared submenus use the agreed English keys.
- [ ] No `i18n-ignore` left on text that only waited for text values (SDK 1.5.11): menu items with data, `[string]` models, nested reasons, lists.
- [ ] `minPlayerVersion` is `0.4.3`; `vestra-plugin check`, `build` and `test` pass.

## How-to: Test a plugin

**Goal:** tests that run with `npm test` on any machine, without the player, and check what a user would see: the menu items, the window's values, the on-screen messages and what happens when the player refuses a call.

`@vestra-player/sdk/testing` runs the plugin against TestHost, a fake player in memory that speaks the real protocol, so the SDK's own logic (revisions, conditional commits, recovery after lost replies) runs as it does in the player. Only the player side is simplified: there is no decoding, no Slint rendering and no native window. A window is a record of its properties and callbacks, and a source is a set of facts the test chooses.

The tests live in `tests/*.test.ts` and use `node:test`; `vestra-plugin test` (the `test` script of Getting started) runs them. Import `@vestra-player/sdk/testing` only there, never in the plugin itself.

#### The shape of a test

The test of the Bookmark example: it prepares the source before the plugin starts, opens the window from its command, fires two Slint callbacks and checks the window and the playback position.

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin, TestHost } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

test("mark the position, then jump back to it", async () => {
  const host = new TestHost();
  host.openElsewhere("/movie.mp4");
  host.setSource({ duration: 600, position: 42 });
  const { stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory: new URL("..", import.meta.url),
    host,
  });

  await host.command("bookmark.open").run();
  const window = host.window("bookmark");
  window.emit("mark");
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(window.props.label, "Bookmark: 42.0 s");

  host.setSource({ position: 300 }); // playback moves on
  window.emit("jump");
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(host.source.position, 42);
  await stop();
});
```

Every test follows the same five steps:

1. **Start** the plugin with startPlugin(activate, { directory }). It reads `manifest.json` in `directory` (from `tests/`, `new URL("..", import.meta.url)`), so the declared capabilities apply: a call that needs an undeclared one fails with `capability`, as in the player. It resolves once activation and every registration made during it are done, and rejects when the player would fail the activation (`activate` throws, or a registration made during it fails, for example with `limit`, `conflict` or `invalid`).
2. **Act** the way the user or another plugin would (below).
3. **Wait** with `await host.settle()`.
4. **Assert** on what the host recorded.
5. **Stop** with `await stop()`: the plugin is disposed as when the player stops it (scopes released, stores flushed) and the host's temporary files are removed. Each test creates its own host.

`startPlugin` also returns `plugin`, the object `activate` received, to call the API directly (`plugin.player.state`). Its options: `host` (a host you prepared before activation, as above), `dataDirectory` (an existing folder as `plugin.dataDirectory`, to test a restart), `sessionStorage` (the values of `plugin.storage.session` an earlier run left, to test a restart within one player session), `locale` (play another interface language, see Translate a plugin), and `id` with `capabilities` to start without a `manifest.json`.

#### Act like the user

| To simulate | Call |
| --- | --- |
| choosing a menu item | `await host.command(id).run()`; rejects like the player when the command is disabled or busy |
| pressing a key | `await host.press("Ctrl+B")`; `host.press("Delete", { panel: true })` while the plugin's panel has focus |
| a control in a window | `host.window(id).emit(callback, ...args)` (the id is the file name: `ui/picture.slint` is `picture`) |
| closing a window with its title-bar button | `host.window(id).userClose()` (runs the window's `onClose`, unlike the plugin's own `close()`) |
| a control in the mounted panel | `host.mounted().emit(callback, ...args)` |
| answering a dialog | before the action: `host.dialogAnswers.push(["/media/movie.mkv"])` for a file dialog, `null` for Cancel, `{ confirmed: true, checked: false }` for `dialogs.confirm` |
| another plugin calling `player.next()` | `await host.step("next")` |

`press` follows the player's binding table: the panel's bindings first when `panel` is true, then the global ones, the player's own commands before the plugin's. A disabled command lets the key go on to the next command bound to it (SDK 1.5.12, as player 0.4.3). `press` resolves with what the key did:

- `"ran"`: the first enabled command bound to the key ran;
- `"reason"`: only disabled commands hold the key, and the first one with a `reason` showed it on the OSD (it is in `host.osd`) and ate the key;
- `"passed"`: only disabled commands without a reason hold it; the key goes on to the focused control and nothing runs.

It rejects when nothing is bound to the key or the command it would run is busy. User overrides preset in `host.bindings.overlay` apply, and `host.conflicts` lists keys that several commands declare.

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

test("the key does nothing while no video is open", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory: new URL("..", import.meta.url),
  });
  assert.equal(await host.press("Ctrl+B"), "reason");
  assert.deepEqual(host.osd, ["Open a video first"]);

  host.openElsewhere("/movie.mp4");
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(await host.press("Ctrl+B"), "ran");
  assert.deepEqual(host.conflicts, []);
  await stop();
});
```

#### Simulate the player

The test decides what the player is doing:

- `host.openElsewhere(path, phase?)`: the user or another plugin opened a source (a new source id, then `phase`, `"ready"` by default). Calls the plugin made against the old state now fail with `stale`.
- `host.setSource({ phase, position, duration, paused, audioTracks, … })`: the state changed (the user paused, playback reached the end). Before `startPlugin`, it presets the source the plugin finds at activation.
- `host.setMainWindow({ fullscreen, videoArea })`, `host.setAppearance(theme)`, `host.setPackages(list)`: the main window, the colour scheme, the installed plugins changed.
- Preset data the player would return: `host.stats` (`player.stats()`), `host.chapters`, `host.clipboard.text`, `host.secrets`, `host.systemInfo`, `host.rendering` (the GPU or software choice, see Offer a GPU rendering switch); `host.tools.handle("ffprobe", (args) => ({ stdout }))` makes a tool available and answers its runs.

#### Inject failures

`host.handle(method, fn)` replaces the player's answer to one protocol method until `host.reset(method)`. The handler gets the request parameters and returns the reply, or throws:

- `throw new HostError(code, message)`: the player refuses; the plugin's call rejects with that `code` (one of the codes in the PluginError table).
- `throw new Error(…)`: the reply is lost, and the SDK runs its recovery path.

Method names are the protocol's (`"processing.replace"`, `"system.openPath"`, `"clipboard.writeText"`): `host.calls` lists every request in order, which shows the method an action uses, and `host.sent(method)` the parameters of one method's requests.

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { HostError, startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

test("a refused change is shown and can be retried", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory: new URL("..", import.meta.url),
  });
  host.openElsewhere("/movie.mp4");
  await host.command("picture").run();
  host.handle("processing.replace", () => {
    throw new HostError("unsupported", "no video stream");
  });
  host.window("picture").emit("adjust", "gamma", 20);
  await host.settle();
  assert.match(String(host.window("picture").props["status"]), /^Picture settings failed/);

  host.reset("processing.replace");
  host.window("picture").emit("retry");
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(host.window("picture").props["status"], "Picture settings applied");
  await stop();
});
```

#### Wait before asserting

`await host.settle(ms?)` waits until no request is in flight and the SDK's follow-up update passes ran; with `ms` it also waits that long, so that debounces and timers due by then fire (`host.settle(400)` is past `storage.json`'s 300 ms debounce). Call it after every action that makes the plugin talk to the player, before asserting. `command(id).run()` and `press` already wait.

`settle` waits only for calls to the player. Work the plugin does on its own (reading or parsing a file, a child process, a network request) can finish after `settle` returns on a loaded machine; poll the value you assert on instead:

```ts nocheck
window.emit("load-file"); // the plugin reads and parses the file itself
for (let i = 0; i < 100 && window.props["status-text"] !== expected; i++)
  await host.settle(20);
assert.equal(window.props["status-text"], expected);
```

#### What to assert on

- **Windows and panels:** `host.window(id).props` and `.visible`, `host.mounted().props`. Property names are the Slint (kebab-case) names: `canMark` is `can-mark`.
- **Commands:** `host.command(id).state` (`enabled`, `checked`, `busy`, `reason`), `.declaration` (the English path and bindings as declared), `.display` (the menu as shown).
- **Messages:** `host.osd` (every message shown, oldest first), `host.osdPanel`, `host.confirms` and `host.confirmTexts` (confirmation dialogs), `host.fileDialogs`.
- **Playback and processing:** `host.source` (`position`, `paused`, `loop`, …), `host.processing`, `host.subtitles`, `host.jobs`, `host.exports`.
- **Anything else the plugin sent:** `host.sent(method)`; `host.system.opened`, `host.clipboard`, `host.tools.calls` for the system services.

The host checks what the player checks: the command limits, the property value limits and the menu ids are enforced with the player's numbers, and processing values are validated with the player's ranges (an out-of-range `filter.set` ends in `failed` with `invalid`). Export jobs advance one step on every state query (`queued`, `running`, `completed`).

#### Test a restart

Copy `host.dataDirectory` after the first run and pass it as `dataDirectory` to the second, to check what the plugin stored and restores; the example is on startPlugin, and Remember a window's state between runs is a plugin that needs it.

A restart within one player session (a reload, an upgrade, a crash) keeps plugin.storage.session too. Pass the first run's `host.sessionStorage` as `sessionStorage` to the second run; leave it out to test a fresh player session, where those values are gone:

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { test } from "node:test";
import { startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

test("goes on with the queue after a restart", async () => {
  const first = await startPlugin(activate);
  await first.plugin.storage.session.set("queue", ["a.mkv", "b.mkv"]);
  const kept = first.host.sessionStorage;
  await first.stop();

  const second = await startPlugin(activate, { sessionStorage: kept });
  assert.deepEqual(await second.plugin.storage.session.get("queue"), [
    "a.mkv",
    "b.mkv",
  ]);
  await second.stop();
});
```

Every member of `TestHost` is in the @vestra-player/sdk/testing reference.

## How-to: Publish a plugin

**Goal:** your plugin appears in the player's plugin store, where users install, update and uninstall it.

The store reads the official plugin repository, [vestrasys/vestra-player-plugins](https://github.com/vestrasys/vestra-player-plugins).
