Every change to it is a pull request to its `main` branch, and **a merge is a release**: there are no beta channels, and CI and revocation are the safety net. Every plugin in it is a third-party plugin; only the plugins built into the player are official. The repository's [README](https://github.com/vestrasys/vestra-player-plugins#contributing-a-plugin) and [CONTRIBUTING](https://github.com/vestrasys/vestra-player-plugins/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) hold the full rules; this page is the author's path through them.

#### Two ways in

- **Registered** (the usual way): the source stays in your own public GitHub repository, and you register it with one file in the repository's `registry/`. CI builds the package from the commit you name, as Flathub does.
- **Hosted**: the source lives in the repository's `plugins/<name>/`, and every change is a pull request there. It needs a maintainer's agreement: open an issue first.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Building registered plugins from source is not implemented yet. The registration format, the id rule and the owner check are final and checked by CI, but a registration pull request cannot be merged until the build lands (the repository's README shows the status).

#### 1. Prepare the package

From the plugin folder:

```sh
npx vestra-plugin check   # the manifest and a strict type check
npx vestra-plugin test    # tests/*.test.ts, see Test a plugin
npx vestra-plugin pack    # dist/ and <id>-<version>.vxp
```

Next to `manifest.json` the store needs:

- the display fields in the manifest: `name`, `author`, `punchline`, `description`, `tags`, `license`, `sourceUrl`, optionally `icon`, and `minPlayerVersion` when the plugin needs a newer player than the first one (Manifest has the rules and the version table);
- `README.md` (what the plugin does, how to use it, what it needs, its limits) and `CHANGELOG.md`, at most 256 KiB each: the store shows both;
- tests under `tests/` that pass (Test a plugin);
- only the capabilities the plugin uses: the store lists them on the plugin's page.

#### 2. Choose the id

The id is `<owner>.<name>`, where `<owner>` is the GitHub user or organization that owns the source repository (for a hosted plugin, the owner recorded in the repository's `plugins/owners.toml`), compared without case: `https://github.com/someone/cool-visualizer` publishes ids that start with `someone.`. Letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_` only.

- `vestra.` is reserved for the player's built-in plugins.
- An id is unique in the repository, also against a hosted plugin's and also with different case.
- A changed id is a new plugin to the store: the old id's version history is not carried over.

#### 3. Register the plugin

Push the plugin to your public repository (it may live in a subdirectory) and note the full 40-character id of the commit to publish; a tag such as `v1.0.0` is good practice, but the registration pins the commit. Then fork the plugin repository and add `registry/<id>.toml`:

```text
# registry/someone.cool-visualizer.toml
repository = "https://github.com/someone/cool-visualizer"
commit = "3f2a9c1d4b5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f8091a2b3c"
path = "."            # optional, default "."
owners = ["someone"]
```

| Key | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| file name | the plugin id plus `.toml`; equals `id` in the manifest |
| `repository` | `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>`, no trailing `/` or `.git`; `<owner>` is the id's prefix |
| `commit` | the full 40-digit lowercase commit id to build |
| `path` | the folder that holds `manifest.json`, relative, no `..` |
| `owners` | the GitHub logins allowed to change or remove this file later; must include you |

No other keys. `npm ci && npm run registry` in the plugin repository checks the file.

A hosted plugin instead adds its folder under `plugins/` (manifest, sources, `tests/`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`) and its owner to `plugins/owners.toml`, after the maintainers agreed in the issue; `npm run plugin -- check <name>` (and `test`, `pack`) run the checks there.

#### 4. Open the pull request

Title it `Add someone.cool-visualizer` (or `Update someone.cool-visualizer to 1.2.0`) and fill in the pull request checklist. On the pull request:

- **Registry owners** checks that you are in `owners` of a new registration, or already an owner of the one you change. It runs the base branch's script and never runs your code.
- **CI** validates the file and runs the publish flow without publishing; for a hosted plugin it also type checks, tests and packs the plugin on macOS, Windows and Linux.
- **Review:** a maintainer reads the source at the registered commit (for an update, the diff since the previous one) and merges, or answers in the pull request.

After the merge, the repository's publish workflow builds the package, releases it as `<id>-v<version>`, signs the index and deploys it; the store shows the plugin at its next refresh.

#### Update, withdraw, revoke

- **Update:** bump `version` in the manifest, add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry, commit, and open a pull request that changes `commit` (a hosted plugin: the pull request with the change). A version is published once and never rebuilt: a change without a new version does not reach users, and a version is never reused or lowered.
- **Owners:** after the first merge only an owner listed on `main` may change or remove the registration, including the list of owners; a maintainer can step in for an abandoned one.
- **Withdraw:** an owner opens a pull request that deletes the registration file. The plugin drops out of the next index, so the store no longer offers it or checks it for updates; copies already installed stay installed (revocations still reach them), and the released packages stay downloadable.
- **Revoke:** for a version that is broken or harmful, an owner asks a maintainer for an entry in the repository's `revoked.json`: the plugin id, the versions (`1.2.0`, or a range such as `>=1.0.0 <1.2.0`) and a reason of up to 500 characters, shown to users. Entries are never removed or edited once merged, so fix a mistake with a new version. The store disables an installed version that matches, tells the user why, and offers the fixed version when there is one; a user who enables it again is asked to confirm the risk first.

#### What users see in the store

The store shows the newest version's manifest fields, so what you write there is the plugin's page:

- **The list**: name and version, author and repository, the punchline. Search covers the name, id, author, punchline and tags; the list can be filtered by tag and sorted by name or by the date of the newest version. There are no download counts.
- **The plugin's page**: the icon, name, author, punchline and the buttons (install, update, uninstall). Three tabs show the README, the changelog and the version history (version, release date, `minPlayerVersion`, and whether the version is current, incompatible or revoked). The player keeps no previous version, and the store has no action to install an older one: a user who wants an older version uninstalls the plugin and installs that version's `.vxp` (Migrating off package rollback). A side column shows the version, the date, the license, a link to `sourceUrl` and the capabilities in plain words, the risky ones highlighted (the wording is the "Shown in the store as" column of Capabilities), with a fixed note that capabilities limit only the player API, not file or network access.
- **Before installing**, the user confirms a dialog that lists the capabilities; an update that adds capabilities lists the new ones. A plugin whose every version needs a newer player shows "needs Vestra Player x.y.z or later" instead of an install button.
- **The README** is rendered as Markdown; relative links and images resolve against the README's own address, and remote images are shown for the official repository.

## How-to: Migrating off package rollback (1.5.16, removed in 1.5.17)

For plugins that manage other plugins (`plugins.manage`): stores, plugin managers, anything that called `packages.rollback` or read `PluginInfo.previousVersion`. Both were deprecated in 1.5.16 and **removed in 1.5.17**: with 1.5.17 a remaining use is a TypeScript compile error. A plugin that only uses its own API needs no change.

#### What changed

The player no longer keeps a previous version of a plugin. An upgrade replaces the package, so there is nothing to roll back to:

- There is no `packages.rollback`: the player answers the wire method with `unsupported` ("unknown package method"), and SDK 1.5.17 no longer has it.
- `packages.list()` and `packages.onChange` entries have no `previousVersion` (always `null` with SDK 1.5.16, removed in 1.5.17).
- Built-in plugins (`builtin: true`) run in place from the player installation. Users manage only third-party plugins: a built-in can be neither uninstalled, replaced nor (from SDK 1.5.18 and the players released with it) disabled; `uninstall` and `setEnabled(id, false)` fail with `unsupported`, and a built-in an older player let the user disable runs again after the upgrade. A built-in's `directory` is inside the installation (`<install resources>/plugins/<id>`) and read-only.
- Third-party plugins can still be uninstalled.

Why: built-ins now run from the read-only installation instead of a copy, and an upgrade replaces the package instead of keeping the old one beside it. Going back to an older version becomes an ordinary uninstall and install that the user starts.

`TestHost` behaves the same way, so tests show it too.

#### 1. Remove rollback calls and `previousVersion` checks

Before:

```ts nocheck
if (info.previousVersion !== null)
  showButton("Roll back", () => plugin.packages.rollback(info.id));
```

After: delete both. There is no replacement call; nothing on the player can restore an earlier package. Remove the button, menu item or command, and any state, text or test that depends on `previousVersion`. With SDK 1.5.17 the compiler finds every remaining use.

#### 2. Going back to an older version

Managing third-party plugins has exactly three operations: **install**, **uninstall** and **disable/enable**. Built-ins have none of them. There is no rollback, no "install older version" and no "Undo install".

To go back to an older version, the user uninstalls the plugin and installs the older version's `.vxp` file themselves, as two ordinary operations. Do not offer an action that does both, an older-version install from a store, or an "Undo" after an install (the official store and the AI window drop theirs). Uninstalling without `removeData` keeps the plugin's data, and a reinstall from the same source reconnects to it; a `.vxp` file is a different source from a repository, so a plugin first installed from the store gets a new, empty data directory.

#### 3. Remove "Undo install"

Remove any Undo action after an install, its texts and translations, and the code that only served it: copies of installed `.vxp` files, remembered "last install" state, and tests of it. A user who wants a plugin gone uninstalls it.

#### 4. Built-in plugins

Check `builtin` before offering actions:

```ts
for (const info of await plugin.packages.list()) {
  const actions = info.builtin
    ? []
    : [info.state === "disabled" ? "Enable" : "Disable", "Uninstall"];
  console.log(info.id, actions);
}
```

- Offer no action for a built-in: never disable, uninstall or install over it (the player answers `unsupported`). Built-ins that an older player listed as `disabled` come back as running.
- Never write into a built-in's `directory`, or into any plugin's `directory`: read `manifest.json` from it if you need to. A plugin writes only under its own plugin.dataDirectory.

#### 5. Tests

With SDK 1.5.17, `host.packages` entries have no `previousVersion` field: delete `previousVersion: null` (or any value) from test data, or the test no longer compiles. `TestHost` has no `packages.rollback`. Remove tests that exercised a rollback; there is nothing left to assert. (With 1.5.16 the field was still required but ignored, and `TestHost` answered rollback with `unsupported`.)

#### Timeline

| SDK    | Player        | What happens                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ------ | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1.5.16 | ships with it | `Packages.rollback` and `PluginInfo.previousVersion` (and the wire field) are `@deprecated`. The player and `TestHost` answer rollback with `unsupported` and list `previousVersion: null`. Code still compiles.                                                                                                              |
| 1.5.17 | ships with it | **Removed:** `Packages.rollback`, `PluginInfo.previousVersion`, the wire method `packages.rollback` and the wire field `previousVersion`, `TestHost`'s `previousVersion` field and its `packages.rollback` handler, and `Packages.rollback` in the `plugins.manage` capability. Remaining uses are TypeScript compile errors. |
| 1.5.18 | ships with it | Built-ins can no longer be disabled: the player and `TestHost` answer `setEnabled(builtin, false)` with `unsupported` (user ruling 2026-10-26).                                                                                                                                                                               |

`apiVersion` stays `vestra/1` in both releases, as when 1.5.8 removed `PackageCandidate.trial()`.

#### Before you hand it in

- [ ] No call to `packages.rollback`; no UI or logic gated on `previousVersion`.
- [ ] Built-ins offer no Disable, Enable or Uninstall.
- [ ] Nothing writes into a plugin's `directory`.
- [ ] No Undo after an install, no older-version install; older versions go through uninstall and a user-chosen `.vxp`.
- [ ] Tests compile and pass with SDK 1.5.17; no `previousVersion` is left in `host.packages` test data.

## Guideline: Interface guidelines

These are the rules the player's built-in plugins follow for their windows, panels and messages. Follow them and your plugin looks like part of the player. They assume you know the five surfaces from Windows, panels, settings pages, dialogs and the OSD; token names, sizes, fonts, icons and widgets are listed in Theme.

All sizes are logical pixels (Slint `px`).

#### Choose the smallest surface

- **Feedback is an OSD message, not a window.** Confirm what just happened with osd.show ("Bookmark added", a new volume, a new speed). Do not open a dialog to say that something succeeded: the player's own snapshot command saves at once and shows a message; only "Save As…" asks.
- **Errors are messages too.** A failed load or a failed action shows one sentence in the OSD; in a window the user is working in, a failure state is drawn in `Theme.danger`.
- **No permanent text over the video.** Nothing sits above the video, and diagnostic numbers are not always on: show them in an OSD info block (osd.panel) behind a command with a check mark, off by default (the player's "Playback Info", Tab, works this way).
- **A dialog only for a real question** (before something destructive) or a path (the system file dialogs). See Choosing a surface.

#### Theme

- **Use `Theme` tokens for every colour**, never a colour value: hard-coded colours do not follow the user's palette (`vestra` dark or `vestra-light`). `Theme.danger` is for failure states and destructive buttons, `Theme.playing` for what is playing now, `Theme.accent` for hover, "on" and selection marks, `Theme.accent-fill` for progress-like fills (sliders, levels).
- **Over the video, use the OSD's colours.** The video area is dark in both palettes, so text and icons drawn on it (a backdrop, an overlay) are white (`#ffffff`) on a translucent dark plate (`#0b0a10c4`), not `Theme.text`, which is dark in `vestra-light`.
- **A check mark on an accent background is white**, in both palettes.
- **Do not set a font family.** Every window uses the system UI font, and Slint falls back per character (CJK included); a fixed family breaks scripts it lacks. For code or aligned numbers use `Theme.font-mono`.
- **Use the four font sizes only**: `Theme.font-xs` (tiny labels), `Theme.font-body` (body text, lists, times), `Theme.font-tab` (tabs, menus), `Theme.font-title` (window and tab titles). Times and counters use tabular digits (`font-feature: tnum`) so they do not jitter.
- **Do not change `Palette.color-scheme`.** The player switches the `std-widgets.slint` controls between their dark and light colours with the palette.

#### Icons

- **Icons come from `@vestra/icons.slint`.** Never use a font character as an icon (✓ › ▲ ▼ ▾ × ▶): each system's font draws it differently.
- **Icon colours follow the state**: normal `Theme.text` (or `Theme.text-dim` for small icons), hover or on `Theme.accent`, pressed `Theme.accent-press`, disabled `Theme.icon-disabled`.
- An icon is drawn in its own box, which is its default size; keep it, so rows and buttons line up with the player's.
- For an icon of your own, draw it the same way: lines only, never filled, round caps and joins, 1.5px wide (1.25px for icons of 12px or less), kept inside the box.

#### Controls

- **Use the player's widgets** from `@vestra/widgets.slint`: `Button` (21px high; `small` 18px), `Slider` (the bottom bar style, or `panel: true` in tool windows), `ToolTipArea`, `UrlInputRow`. They take their sizes and colours from `Theme`. Other controls come from `std-widgets.slint`.
- **Control sizes are tokens**: `Theme.button-height`, `Theme.button-primary-height` (the main action at the bottom of a dialog), `Theme.button-small-height` (a "Default" button in a row), `Theme.input-height`, `Theme.checkbox-row-height`, `Theme.label-height`, `Theme.form-row-gap`, `Theme.dialog-padding`.
- **Corners**: `Theme.radius-control` for buttons, rows, hover plates and tooltips; `Theme.radius-panel` for menus, floating layers and larger plates.
- **Icon buttons have no separators between them.** Hover and press light a rounded plate behind the icon (`Theme.hover-bg`, `Theme.press-bg`).
- **Explain icon buttons with a tooltip** (`ToolTipArea`), and put long values (a full path) in a tooltip instead of a line of text.

#### Tool windows

- **No heading inside the window.** The title bar already shows the window's `title`.
- **Theme sizes throughout**: buttons and inputs 21px, form rows 24–26px apart, padding 8–14px, body text `Theme.font-body`.
- **Adjustments apply at once.** A window that changes picture, sound or subtitles has no "Apply" or "OK": every change takes effect while the user moves the control, and each row has its own "Default" button that resets it. Keep the slider responsive while dragging (the slider guide).
- **Status and error text is one sentence**, written as English source text and translated like every other text (Translate a plugin). Never show debugging details: task ids, revisions, generations, stack traces.
- **Closing a tool window does not undo its effect.** The window is a way to change a setting, not the setting's owner.

##### Small adjustment windows

The player's picture, audio and subtitle tools share one layout; a window of the same kind uses it too:

| Part                          | Size and style                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Window                        | 301 wide, at most 320 × 280; background `Theme.bg-bar`; content 8 from the left and right edges (285 usable)                                |
| Tabs (if any)                 | 31 high, 74 wide, text `Theme.font-tab` in `Theme.text-dim`; the current tab in `Theme.text` with a short `Theme.accent-fill` line under it |
| Page                          | background `Theme.bg-panel`                                                                                                                 |
| Row                           | 24 high: label 65 wide, right-aligned, `Theme.font-body`; `Slider` with `panel: true`, 154 × 12; a small "Default" button, 41 × 18          |
| Toggle buttons (flip, rotate) | 46 × 22; choice buttons 51 × 22 (69 wide for longer labels)                                                                                 |

##### Dialog-like windows

- **A link input is `UrlInputRow`**: the input with **Open** and **Cancel**, Enter accepts and Escape cancels, no history list. The player's own link windows (Open URL, the playlist's Add URL, the plugin store) all use it.
- **Group the fields** of a longer form (storage, format and size, range…) with labels in a right-aligned left column; the main action is a primary button (`Theme.button-primary-height`) at the bottom.
- The standard close keys close every tool window; you cannot and need not handle them.

#### Panels

- **A sidebar panel has no heading of its own.** The player shows its title in the sidebar's tab strip when there are two or more panels; with one panel there is no strip.
- **No status or path lines in a panel.** Messages go to the OSD; a full path is a tooltip on its row.
- **Show state with colour, not words.** As in the player's playlist: what is playing in `Theme.playing` (with a 2px bar at the left), what was played in `Theme.text-played`, the selection on `Theme.selected-bg`. A failed item gets the `failed` icon at the end of its row and an OSD message.
- **Lists are plain**: single-line rows, background `Theme.bg-list`, no cards, no stripes, no rounded rows; scroll bars come from `std-widgets.slint` so they follow the palette.
- **Commands of a panel go into its right-click menu**, made of the plugin's commands (panel.showMenu); see Menus.
- **The bottom bar is icons only**: no text buttons, no source path, no status text (the source name is in the window title, status is an OSD message).

##### Writing a bottom bar

The bottom bar holds one panel, and every plugin's command buttons (CommandOptions.button) and the player's sidebar toggle show inside it, in a strip the player fills. A bar that replaces the built-in one (`vestra.playback`) must place that strip, or those buttons show nowhere while it is mounted (their menu entries stay):

- **Place `BarButtons`** from `@vestra/bar-buttons.slint` at the right end of the button row, and give it `room`: the width left after your own controls. It shows as many 41×40 cells as fit and loses them from its outer (left) end inward: of the plugins' buttons the lowest order goes first, and the sidebar toggle goes last. The strip is as wide as the cells it shows, so lay your controls out against its `width`. Do not put it under an `if`: it must exist for the player to see it placed. `first-shown` (out) is the index of the leftmost plugin button shown, if your layout needs it.
- **Decide what goes first when the window narrows.** The built-in bar gives the strip only the room its own buttons and the time leave, so the strip shrinks first, then its Fullscreen button hides, and the time is never cut.
- **Do not draw a sidebar toggle of your own**: the strip has the player's (**Toggle Sidebar**, `host/sidebar`), with its state.
- `vestra-plugin check` warns when a plugin mounts a bottom bar whose Slint file does not import `BarButtons` from `@vestra/bar-buttons.slint`, itself or through the plugin's own Slint files it imports, and the player logs the buttons a mounted bar hides.

```slint
import { BarButtons } from "@vestra/bar-buttons.slint";

export component MyBar inherits Rectangle {
    height: 40px;
    // Your controls on the left, 3 × 41px wide …
    strip := BarButtons {
        x: root.width - self.width - 4px;
        y: 0px;
        room: max(0px, root.width - 3 * 41px - 8px);
    }
}
```

#### Text

- **Every visible text is English source text** that the player translates (Translate a plugin). Write short, plain sentences; one sentence per status or error.
- **Leave room for longer languages.** German and French texts are usually longer than English; a Chinese, Japanese or Korean character is about one font size wide, a Latin letter about half. Let labels and buttons grow with their text (layouts, `preferred-width`; the `Button` widget does) instead of fixing widths to the English text.
- **Mixed scripts must render without boxes.** That is why you use the system font (above): the player falls back per character to the system's fonts (on Windows also to a bundled CJK font) (Theme).
- **Data is not translated.** File names, track names and device names show as they are.

#### Check your plugin

- Switch the palette (Settings ▸ Appearance) with your windows open: everything should follow at once.
- Switch the interface language (Settings ▸ Language, used from the next start) to German and to Japanese, and look for clipped or overlapping text.
- Compare your tool window with the player's Picture Adjustments window: same row heights, same buttons, same slider.

## Guideline: Menu guidelines

The player has one menu, opened with a right click on the video. There is no menu button in the window and no menu bar at the top of the screen, so every command a user may look for is in this menu or in a panel's right-click menu. It is merged from the commands of every plugin and the player's own; these rules keep the result one menu instead of a pile of plugins.

How paths merge, how `order` and `group` sort items and how a key finds its command are explained in Commands, menus and key bindings. Menu ids, the shared menu keys, the binding syntax and the keys the system takes first are listed in Commands. The declaration itself is CommandOptions.

#### Organize by what the user does

- **Put a command where its subject is, not under your plugin's name.** A video filter goes into Video, a subtitle tool into Subtitles, an open-something command into Open. A plugin that brings a domain of its own gets a submenu named after the domain, not after the plugin (Games for an emulator, not the emulator's name).
- **Before adding an item, look for an existing one.** Every command the player and its built-in plugins add, with its menu path and default key, is listed in Built-in commands. Do not add a second entry for something the player already does, and do not scatter one feature over several menus.
- **Top level is for frequent, direct commands**: opening files, closing, fullscreen and the entries that show a window or panel. Everything else goes into a submenu of its domain.
- **No "File" or "View" menu.** Commands that open something go into Open ▸; commands that show a window or panel sit directly at the top level.

#### The top level

The top level as the player ships it (shortcuts in the Windows notation; the menu shows each system's own):

```text
Open File…                    Ctrl+O, F3   group open
Open ▸
Close                         F4
Reopen Current/Last File      Ctrl+Y
Copy to Clipboard ▸
────────────────────────────────────────
Playback ▸                                 group domain
Subtitles ▸
Video ▸
Audio ▸
────────────────────────────────────────
Toggle Fullscreen             Enter        group screen
Screen ▸
────────────────────────────────────────
Playlist  ✓                   F6           group windows
Playback Info  ✓              Tab
Playback Properties…          Ctrl+F1
Vestra Player AI…
Plugin Store…
────────────────────────────────────────
Settings ▸
────────────────────────────────────────
About Vestra Player…          F1
────────────────────────────────────────
Quit                          Cmd+Q        group exit
```

A top-level item uses the group and the `order` range of its kind:

| Group                  | `order` | For                                                                              |
| ---------------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `open`                 | 100–199 | Opening and closing sources                                                      |
| `domain` (the default) | 200–699 | Domain submenus: Playback, Subtitles, Video, Audio, and a new domain of your own |
| `screen`               | 700–799 | Fullscreen and the window's size and placement                                   |
| `windows`              | 800–899 | Items that show a window or a panel (a check mark when it toggles one)           |
| `exit`                 | 900–999 | Quit                                                                             |

Keep a group's orders contiguous: `group` only draws a separator between neighbours of different groups, so an item whose order falls into another group's range splits that group in two.

#### Inside a built-in menu

- **Name the menu by its id**: `["@video", "Blur"]`. The seven built-in menus (Open, Playback, Subtitles, Video, Audio, Screen, Settings) stay where they are whatever you put in them.
- **Without an `order`, your item goes to the end** of the menu, after the player's own items, which is usually right for a plugin. To sit next to a related player item, give an `order` near that item's; the player's items use 100 and up, in the order listed in Built-in commands, and the ranges per menu are at CommandOptions.order.
- **Group related items** with a `group` of your own, so a separator sets them apart from the player's items.
- **Playback ▸ Speed and Playback ▸ Seek are the player's.** You can add to them; their titles stay the player's.

#### Shared submenus

- **Write a shared submenu exactly as the menu keys list does.** Menus merge by the English words of the path: `["@playback", "Chapters and Bookmarks", …]` joins the existing submenu, `["@playback", "Bookmarks", …]` makes a second one. The keys are in Commands.
- **A new submenu that other plugins should use is a new menu key**: ask the player's maintainers to register it instead of inventing it in one plugin, so it appears in the list.
- **A submenu's title is translated by the catalog of the plugin that declares its first command**; your own submenu therefore needs its words in your catalog.
- **Menu paths are written with `▸`** (U+25B8) in documentation and messages, never `▶`, which many systems draw as an emoji.

#### Titles

- **Title Case**, short: "Save Current Frame", "Show Marks on Seek Bar". A menu is as wide as its longest title in the user's language; a CJK character counts about twice a Latin letter, and German or French titles are longer than English, so a long title widens the whole menu.
- **End with `…`** (one character, U+2026) when the item opens a window or asks something before acting ("Adjust Sync…", "Plugin Store…"); no `…` when it acts at once.
- **A toggle has a check mark** (`checked: true | false`, as "Show Subtitles"). **Mutually exclusive choices are radio items** (`radio: true`) in one group: speeds, loop modes, snapshot formats, palettes.
- **Do not put key names in a title.** The menu shows each item's binding on the right, in the system's notation.
- **Dynamic items are data.** Track names, device names, file names and bookmarks are shown as they are, not translated. Cap long dynamic lists well below the command limit (Limits): the player shows at most 50 chapters and ends the list with "More Chapters… (N in all)".
- **Keep unavailable items, disabled, with a reason** (`enabled: false` and `reason`) instead of removing them; remove an item only when it can never apply here (the player's Picture-in-Picture item exists only where the system supports it). An empty dynamic list shows one disabled item that says so ("No Audio Tracks").

#### A panel's right-click menu

- **A panel's commands go into its own right-click menu** (panel.showMenu), not into the main menu: it looks the same and is made of the plugin's own commands. Commands that make sense only in the panel have no `path` there.
- **Keys that act on the panel's content** (Enter to play, Delete to remove) are bindings with `focus: "panel"`: they win over the global meaning of the same key while the panel has focus, and give it back when it loses focus. That is intended, not a conflict.
- The player's playlist is the model: its list menu, its Add and Sort buttons and its panel keys; its panel keys are at the end of Built-in commands.

#### Default bindings

A default binding is optional. Users rebind every command (Settings ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts…) and can turn all defaults off (Settings ▸ Ignore Default Shortcuts), so give one only to a command people repeat often.

- **Pick an unused key.** Check Built-in commands, which lists every default binding of the player and its built-in plugins. Two commands with the same key are not an error, but only one of them runs (the user's choice, then the player's own commands, then the plugin loaded first), so a colliding default simply does nothing for the user.
- **Write `Ctrl`, not `Cmd`**, for a binding that works on both systems: on macOS `Ctrl+X` fires for both ⌃X and ⌘X.
- **Avoid the keys the system takes first**, the standard close keys among them, as defaults.
- **The right mouse button opens the menu** and is not a binding input; the other video-area mouse inputs are.
- **A typed symbol is its own key**: `>` is not `Shift+.`, so `.` and `>` can do different things.
- **Remember that bindings belong to the main window.** They do not fire while a tool window or the Options window has focus (Focus and keyboard).

## Reference: Manifest

`manifest.json` sits at the root of the plugin directory and of the package. The player and every `vestra-plugin` command check it against the same rules: an unknown field, an unknown capability, a field that breaks its rule, or a path that leaves the package (symbolic links included) is refused.

```json
{
  "id": "me.bookmark",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "ui.window"],
  "name": "Bookmark",
  "punchline": "Mark a moment and jump back to it.",
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.4.3"
}
```

#### Fields

**Kind**: *required* fields every plugin has (`version` may come from `package.json` at build time); *display* fields are optional and shown by the plugin store and the plugin manager (player 0.2.0); *optional* changes how the player loads the plugin.

| Field | Kind | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | required | 1–128 bytes of ASCII letters, digits and `.`, `-`, `_`. Ids `vestra` and `vestra.…` (any case) belong to the player's built-in plugins; installing one fails with `reserved`. A plugin in the official plugin repository is named `<GitHub user or organization>.<plugin>`; `vestra-plugin check` only hints at a missing prefix. |
| `version` | required in the package | `x.y.z`, three whole numbers. `vestra-plugin build` writes it into `dist/manifest.json` from `--version`, the manifest or `package.json`. |
| `apiVersion` | required | `vestra/1`. |
| `entry` | required | Path of the entry module inside the package: `.ts` while developing, `.js` after `build`. |
| `capabilities` | required | Capabilities from Capabilities, each at most once. |
| `name` | display | 1–64 characters, one line, no leading or trailing white space. English; translated with the plugin's catalog. |
| `author` | display | 1–64 characters, one line. |
| `punchline` | display | One-line summary, 1–120 characters. English; translated. |
| `description` | display | Plain text, 1–2000 characters; line breaks allowed. English; translated. |
| `tags` | display | At most 8 tags, each 1–24 characters on one line, unique ignoring case. English; translated. |
| `icon` | display | Package path of a PNG or JPEG (by content), at most 512 KiB and 1024 pixels per side; 256×256 recommended. |
| `readme` | display | Package path of a UTF-8 `.md` file of at most 256 KiB, shown on the store page. Default: `README.md` when the package has one. |
| `changelog` | display | The same rules; default `CHANGELOG.md` when present. |
| `sourceUrl` | display | An `https:` address of at most 2048 bytes. |
| `license` | display | 1–64 characters, preferably an SPDX expression such as `MIT`. |
| `minPlayerVersion` | optional | `x.y.z`: the oldest player that loads the plugin (compared with `plugin.app.version`, three numbers). An older player refuses it with `versionMismatch` ("requires Vestra Player ≥ x.y.z") before it reads anything else, so a manifest with newer fields fails with that, not with an unknown field. See Player versions. |

- `name`, `punchline`, `description` and `tags` are English source text; the player shows them translated with the plugin's own catalog (Translate a plugin) through PluginInfo.
- An `icon`, `readme` or `changelog` that is named but missing is refused. `vestra-plugin build` copies them (and a default `README.md` or `CHANGELOG.md`) into the package: the README is the plugin's page in the store, so write it for users.
- A call to a member whose capability is not declared fails with code `capability` (Capabilities).

#### Player versions

The SDK's major version follows the plugin API: every 1.x release implements `apiVersion` `vestra/1`, minor releases only add to it, and a breaking change gets a new `apiVersion` and a new major version. Some additions also need a newer player. A plugin that uses one sets `minPlayerVersion` to the highest version it needs; an older player then refuses it with `versionMismatch` instead of failing at the first call.

The table lists the API whose documentation names a player version, newest last:

| Player | API that needs it or changed with it |
| --- | --- |
| 0.2.0 | Plugin.dataDirectory, MarkdownRef, Ui.markdown, PackageManifest, Packages.validateArchive |
| 0.3.0 | CommandOptions, MENU_IDS |
| 0.4.0 | ThemeId |
| 0.4.1 | PluginError, FileResolverOptions, PackageCandidate.install, PluginWarning.code, Packages.validate |
| 0.4.2 | Resolvers.fileTypes, Resolvers.onFileTypesChange |
| 0.4.3 | CommandOptions.path, PropValue, View.set, Appearance.setLanguage, TemplateArgs, Text, ConfirmOptions.args, OsdPanel.set, OsdPanelOptions.maxColumns, Osd.show |
| 0.5.1 | ImageRef, ImageOptions.maxSide, PropValue, Ui.image, Ui.remoteImage, SlotState.reason, Panel.setInteraction, PlaybackStats.presentedFps, Player.setStepSeek, Host.run, Packages.reload |
| 0.5.2 | HostAction |
| 0.5.3 | Scrub.seek |
| 0.5.5 | SessionStorage |
| 0.5.10 | CommandButton, CommandOptions.button |
| 0.5.12 | SystemInfo.rendering |
| 0.5.13 | SystemInfo.renderingReason, RenderingMode, RenderingPreference, RenderingReasonCode, RenderingReason, RenderingState, Rendering |

The Slint library carries no version tags: `Theme.danger` needs player 0.3.0; `@vestra/icons.slint` and the palette `vestra-light` need 0.4.0 (Theme).

`@vestra-player/sdk/runtime` is the player's own entry point and is not covered by these rules. What changed in each SDK release is in the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/vestrasys/vestra-player-sdk/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Reference: Capabilities

A plugin lists what it may do in the manifest's `capabilities` (Manifest). A call to a member whose capability is missing fails with code `capability`; nothing else is checked at run time, and capabilities limit only the player API, not the file system or the network (a plugin is a Node.js process). The store shows the capabilities to the user before installing, in the words of the "Shown in the store as" column; the highlighted ones reach outside the plugin's own features.

| Capability | Opens | Also needs | Shown in the store as | Highlighted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `producer.av` | Player.openStream | `playback.control` | Provide audio and video it generates itself |  |
| `playback.read` | Player.state, Player.refresh, Player.stats, Player.chapters, Player.audioDevices, Timeline.marks | — | Read what is playing and the position |  |
| `playback.control` | Player.open, Player.setPaused, Player.seek, Player.setRate, Player.restart, Player.close, Player.scrub, Player.setOutput, Player.provideSequence, Player.next, Player.previous, Player.addAudioTrack, Player.selectAudioTrack, Player.step, Player.setStepSeek, Player.setLoop, Player.setAudioDevice, Power.preventSleep | — | Open media, control playback, keep the computer awake |  |
| `source.resolve` | Resolvers.add | — | Resolve online video addresses |  |
| `events` | Player.onChange, Subtitles.onChange, Timeline.onChange, MainWindow.onChange, Appearance.onChange, PanelSlot.onChange, Panel.onChange, BackdropSlot.onChange, Resolvers.onFileTypesChange | — | Receive playback changes as they happen |  |
| `commands` | Commands.add, Host.run | — | Add menu commands and shortcuts |  |
| `ui.window` | Windows.create | — | Open tool windows |  |
| `ui.mount` | Panels.mount, Panels.bottom, Panels.sidebar, Panels.backdrop, PanelSlot.onChange, Panel.onChange, BackdropSlot.onChange | — | Show panels in the bottom bar, the sidebar or behind the video |  |
| `ui.dialog` | Dialogs.confirm, Dialogs.openFile, Dialogs.openFiles, Dialogs.openDirectory, Dialogs.saveFile | — | Show file pickers and confirmations |  |
| `plugins.manage` | Packages.validate, Packages.validateArchive, Packages.setEnabled, Packages.reload, Packages.uninstall | — | Install, uninstall and disable other plugins | yes |
| `processing.video` | Plugin.video.filter, Plugin.video.view, Plugin.video.render | `playback.read` | Process the picture (filters, shaders) |  |
| `processing.audio` | Plugin.audio.filter | `playback.read`, `events` | Process the sound |  |
| `subtitles.read` | Subtitles.state, Subtitles.onChange, Subtitles.refresh | — | Read subtitles |  |
| `subtitles.control` | Subtitles.select, Subtitles.load, Subtitles.remove, Subtitles.setStyle | — | Load and change subtitles |  |
| `media.read` | MediaCapture.capture, Snapshot.export | `media.control` | Take snapshots and export clips |  |
| `media.control` | MediaCapture.capture, Snapshot.export | `media.read` | Take snapshots and export clips |  |
| `ui.osd` | Osd.show, Osd.panel | — | Show messages on the video |  |
| `clipboard` | Clipboard.readText, Clipboard.writeText, Clipboard.writeImage | — | Read and write the clipboard | yes |
| `window.control` | MainWindow.setVideoArea, MainWindow.setAlwaysOnTop, MainWindow.setCursorAutoHide, MainWindow.setPictureInPicture | — | Adjust the main window (size, on top, picture-in-picture) |  |
| `bindings.manage` | Bindings.list, Bindings.set, Bindings.reset, Bindings.onChange | — | Change all shortcuts | yes |
| `timeline.marks` | Timeline.layer | — | Show marks on the progress bar |  |
| `ui.drop` | Drops.provide, Panel.onDrop | — | Receive files dropped on the player |  |
| `ui.settings` | Settings.page, Settings.show | — | Add pages to the Options window |  |
| `ui.theme` | Appearance.set, Appearance.setLanguage | — | Change the player's palette |  |
| `secrets` | Secrets.get, Secrets.set, Secrets.delete | — | Store sign-in details in the system keychain | yes |
| `rendering.manage` | Rendering.setPreference, Rendering.restartPlayer | — | Choose GPU or software rendering and restart the player | yes |

**Also needs** applies to every member of the row: declare those capabilities as well. A few members or options need one more, documented at the member:

- video.filter also needs `events`.
- The changes of Subtitles (`select`, `load`, `remove`, `setStyle`) also need `subtitles.read`: they read the current selection first.
- A `processed` snapshot or export (MediaCapture) also needs `playback.read` and `subtitles.read`.
- A file resolver (Resolvers.add with file types) also needs `producer.av`.
- Without `events`, Player.state is read at start and after the plugin's own operations, and `onChange` listeners do not fire for changes made elsewhere.

#### Without a capability

A member not in the table needs no capability: `plugin.tools`, `plugin.storage`, `plugin.system`, `plugin.app`, `plugin.ui` (images and Markdown), `plugin.i18n`, reading window.state, appearance.theme, packages.list and rendering.state. The table is `CAPABILITY_INFO`, which tests can import from `@vestra-player/sdk/testing` to check a manifest (CAPABILITY_INFO).

#### Catching a missing capability

The player refuses a request whose capability the manifest does not declare, at run time. The SDK finds such calls earlier, with one rule: the player's own table of which request needs which capability (copied from the player), and the requests each member above sends. Nothing has to be remembered:

| Where                                     | How                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The editor                                | An error at the member, "`Player.seek` needs the capability "playback.control", which manifest.json does not declare", with the quick fix **Add 'playback.control' to manifest.json**. It comes from the TypeScript plugin `@vestra-player/sdk/ts-plugin`, listed in the project's `tsconfig.json` (`"plugins": [{ "name": "@vestra-player/sdk/ts-plugin" }]`, as in Getting started). In VS Code, run **TypeScript: Select TypeScript Version** → **Use Workspace Version**: editors load a project's plugins only with the project's own TypeScript. `tsc` ignores language-service plugins. |
| `vestra-plugin check`, `build` and `pack` | `check` reports each use as `file:line:column` with the member, the capability and the request, and fails; `build` and `pack` run `check` first, so a package cannot be made with a missing capability. `check --json` prints the findings as JSON (Command line).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

The TypeScript plugin runs inside the editor's TypeScript server, on the editor's own Node.js, and needs that Node.js to be version 22.12 or later (the plugin is an ES module loaded with `require()`; the SDK itself needs 26, but the editor brings its own); current VS Code qualifies. With an older one the server logs that it could not load `@vestra-player/sdk/ts-plugin` and the editor shows no capability errors; `vestra-plugin check` still reports them. The quick fix edits the saved `manifest.json` (editors do not share unsaved JSON buffers with the TypeScript server) and keeps its layout and line endings.

The manifest is the nearest `manifest.json` above the file. Only the plugin's own code is checked: `tests/` (tests choose their capabilities in `startPlugin`), `node_modules/`, `dist/` and `vendor/` are not. A member needs the capabilities its requests need and those capabilities' **Also needs**, so a `video.filter` without `playback.read` is reported too.

The check follows types, not names: `plugin.player.seek`, `const { player } = plugin; player.seek(…)`, a function taking a `Player`, `plugin.clipboard["readText"]` and members of objects other members return (`panel.onChange` on a mounted panel) are all found. Not found: access with a computed name (`player[name]`), values typed `any`, plain JavaScript without types, and options that need more than the member (a `processed` capture, a file resolver). The player's check at run time stays: it is the boundary, since a plugin can bypass the SDK.

## Reference: Limits

The player bounds what one request may cost it. The limits are guards against runaway plugins, not sizes to aim for: a plugin that needs to come close to one usually needs a different design (send the rows near the view, not the whole list). The SDK checks the same limits before it sends a request, so a plugin's own tests hit them too (TestHost enforces them). A name in code style is a constant you can import from `@vestra-player/sdk/testing`.

#### Commands

A command added past a limit fails with code `limit` (its `ready` rejects; during activation, activation fails). Commands already registered are unaffected, and disposing one frees its slot at once.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMMAND_LIMITS.perPlugin` | 160 | Commands one plugin instance may have at the same time. |
| `COMMAND_LIMITS.total` | 1024 | Commands of every plugin plus the player's own, together. |

#### Bottom-bar buttons

A command's button (CommandOptions.button, player 0.5.10) past a limit is left out, not refused: the command registers and its menu entry stays, and the player logs the button with `limit`. Each plugin keeps its first declared button; of those, the player keeps the eight highest orders, so the lowest go first, as in a narrow strip (equal orders: the smaller plugin id, then the earlier declaration, goes first). The player's own sidebar toggle is extra.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BAR_BUTTON_LIMITS.perPlugin` | 1 | Buttons one plugin shows. |
| `BAR_BUTTON_LIMITS.total` | 8 | Buttons the player shows, every plugin together, besides its own sidebar toggle. |
| `BAR_BUTTON_LIMITS.maxOrder` | 999 | The highest `order`. |

#### Property values

One value written to a window, panel or settings page property (View.set, View.bind or an initial property). A value over a limit is refused whole with code `limit`; the property keeps what it showed.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `UI_VALUE_LIMITS.depth` | 8 | Nesting depth; the value itself is depth 0. |
| `UI_VALUE_LIMITS.values` | 16384 | Values in all, counting every array, object, string, number, boolean and null, the value itself included; a Markdown document is one. |
| `UI_VALUE_LIMITS.arrayRows` | 4096 | Rows of one array. |
| `UI_VALUE_LIMITS.stringBytes` | 65536 (64 KiB) | UTF-8 bytes of one string or object field name. |
| `UI_VALUE_LIMITS.textBytes` | 1048576 (1 MiB) | UTF-8 bytes of all strings and field names together, the text of the value's Markdown documents included. |

#### Text values

One Text or TextList, with everything nested in it. A text over a limit fails with code `invalid`.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TEXT_LIMITS.depth` | 8 | Nesting depth of texts and lists; the value itself is depth 0. |
| `TEXT_LIMITS.nodes` | 1024 | Texts, lists and arguments in all, the value itself included. |
| `TEXT_LIMITS.args` | 16 | Arguments of one text. |
| `TEXT_LIMITS.items` | 256 | Items of one list. |
| `TEXT_LIMITS.stringBytes` | 4096 (4 KiB) | UTF-8 bytes of a source text or a string argument. |

#### Markdown

plugin.ui.markdown and its image downloads. A failed or oversized image shows its alt text; the call does not fail for it. The number of images per document and of blocks shown are on `Ui.markdown`.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| textBytes | 262144 (256 KiB) | Text bytes. |
| imageBytes | 4194304 (4 MiB) | Bytes of one downloaded image. |
| imageTimeoutMs | 10000 (10 s) | Download time per image. |
| redirects | 5 | Redirects followed per image. |
| concurrency | 4 | Downloads at once, per plugin. |
| cacheBytes | 33554432 (32 MiB) | Cache size per plugin. |
| cacheMaxAgeMs | 86400000 (24 h) | An address is fetched again after this long. |

#### On-screen display

Counted on the text as shown, after translation and with its arguments filled in. A text over a limit fails with code `invalid`: osd.show rejects, OsdPanel.set reports to `Scope.onError`. Font sizes and placement are at Osd.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OSD_LIMITS.messageChars` | 200 | Characters of one `osd.show` message (200; at least 1 that is not white space). Line breaks are shown as spaces. |
| `OSD_LIMITS.panelLines` | 32 | Lines of the information block (`OsdPanel.set`). |
| `OSD_LIMITS.panelBytes` | 4096 (4 KiB) | UTF-8 bytes of the information block. |
| `OSD_LIMITS.minColumns` | 8 | The smallest `OsdPanelOptions.maxColumns`. |
| `OSD_LIMITS.maxColumns` | 1000 | The largest `OsdPanelOptions.maxColumns`. |

#### Secrets

plugin.secrets. A name or value out of its rule fails with code `invalid`; a new name beyond the count fails with `limit`.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SECRET_LIMITS.nameChars` | 64 | Characters of a name (64, at least 1), each one of `a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_` and `-`. |
| `SECRET_LIMITS.valueBytes` | 1024 (1 KiB) | UTF-8 bytes of a value. |
| `SECRET_LIMITS.names` | 256 | Different names one plugin may have stored at the same time. |

#### Session storage

plugin.storage.session (player 0.5.5). A key out of its rule, or a value that is not JSON (or has a string with a lone surrogate), fails with code `invalid`; a `set` that would take the plugin over `bytes` fails with `limit` and changes nothing. Each key counts its UTF-8 bytes, its value as compact JSON and `entryBytes`. One `set` is also one message, so a single value must fit in `MESSAGE_LIMIT` with its key and the request around it.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SESSION_STORAGE_LIMITS.keyBytes` | 1024 (1 KiB) | UTF-8 bytes of a key. |
| `SESSION_STORAGE_LIMITS.bytes` | 1048576 (1 MiB) | Bytes one plugin may hold at the same time: for every key, its UTF-8 bytes, its value written as compact JSON (`JSON.stringify(value)`) and `entryBytes`. |
| `SESSION_STORAGE_LIMITS.entryBytes` | 128 | What each key costs on top of its text and value (128): the player's own bookkeeping, so that many tiny entries stay within `bytes` of memory. |

#### Subtitle files

Subtitles.load uploads a file as a track of the current source. A file over `fileBytes` fails with `invalid`; every other limit fails with `busy` and nothing is loaded. The counts are per source, so another file starts from zero. Removing a track frees its place among the tracks and their bytes, but a load stays counted until the source changes.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SUBTITLE_LIMITS.fileBytes` | 2097152 (2 MiB) | UTF-8 bytes of one file; a larger one fails with `invalid`. |
| `SUBTITLE_LIMITS.tracksPerPlugin` | 4 | Tracks one plugin has loaded into the current source at the same time. |
| `SUBTITLE_LIMITS.tracks` | 16 | Loaded tracks of every plugin in the current source at the same time. |
| `SUBTITLE_LIMITS.totalBytes` | 16777216 (16 MiB) | Bytes of the loaded tracks of every plugin in the current source together. |
| `SUBTITLE_LIMITS.loadsPerPlugin` | 16 | Loads by one plugin into the current source, removed tracks included. |
| `SUBTITLE_LIMITS.loads` | 128 | Loads by every plugin into the current source, removed tracks included. |
| `SUBTITLE_LIMITS.uploadsPerPlugin` | 2 | Loads of one plugin in progress at the same time. |
| `SUBTITLE_LIMITS.uploads` | 8 | Loads of every plugin in progress at the same time. |

#### Messages

Every request a plugin sends travels as one protocol line. The plugin's side refuses a longer one with code `limit` before sending it; property values meet their own limits first.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MESSAGE_LIMIT` | 1048576 (1 MiB) | The longest message a plugin may send the player, in UTF-8 bytes of one protocol line with its newline (1 MiB). The player stops a plugin that writes a longer one, so the plugin's side refuses such a request before sending it: it rejects with code `limit`. Property values meet `UI_VALUE_LIMITS` before this. |

#### Render options

RenderSettings; more shaders fail with `invalid`.

| Limit | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Entries of `RenderSettings.shaders` | 16 | mpv user shaders (`.glsl`): absolute paths of existing files, at most 16, in order. |

#### Limits documented at their API

- Filter chains: the number of nodes across all plugins, one `frameBlend`, and the range of every node's parameters, at VideoFilter; the audio delay at AudioFilter.
- Generated streams: frame sizes and sample values at StreamFrame; a frame that breaks them ends the stream with `invalid`.
- Manifest fields: Manifest.

## Reference: Commands, menus and bindings

The names to look up while declaring a command with plugin.commands.add. How menus merge and how a key finds its command is explained in Commands, menus and key bindings; where a command should go is in Guidelines: menus.

#### Menu paths

A command's `path` is a list of 1 to 8 segments in English source text, the last one the item itself: `["@video", "Snapshot", "Copy Snapshot"]`. This documentation writes a path with `▸`: **Video ▸ Snapshot ▸ Copy Snapshot**. The `▸` is notation only; a segment never contains it.

- Paths merge by these English texts (their **keys**), whatever the interface language, so commands whose paths start with the same keys share a submenu.
- The first segment may name a built-in menu by id (`@video`) or by key (`Video`). Only the first segment is read as an id; an unknown id (`@view`) or an id with nothing after it fails with `invalid`.
- A segment that contains data is a Text; it merges by its English rendering.

#### Built-in menus

| First segment | Or its key |
| --- | --- |
| `@open` | `Open` |
| `@playback` | `Playback` |
| `@subtitles` | `Subtitles` |
| `@video` | `Video` |
| `@audio` | `Audio` |
| `@screen` | `Screen` |
| `@settings` | `Settings` |

Players before 0.3.0 show `@video` as a menu of its own; players up to 0.4.2 titled these menus in Chinese, where only the id form reaches them. The fixed orders of the built-in menus and of the player's own items are on CommandOptions.order.

#### Submenu keys in use

The submenus that exist already, by key path. Write the same keys to add a command to one of them; a near-synonym makes a second submenu.

| Key path | Declared by |
| --- | --- |
| Playback ▸ Speed | the player |

#### Bottom-bar buttons

`button: { icon, order }` on commands.add (CommandButton, SDK 1.5.29, player 0.5.10) gives a command a button in the bottom bar's strip of command buttons (`BarButtons`, Writing a bottom bar).

| Field | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `icon` | A name of the player's icon set (the names in Theme: Icons, `BAR_BUTTON_ICONS`), or an image from plugin.ui.image drawn in the 14×12 icon box in the icon colour (only its alpha counts). Unknown name: `invalid`. |
| `order` | Integer 0–999, left to right ascending; equal orders by plugin id, then declaration order. The built-in plugins use 100 (Vestra Player AI) and 200 (Plugin Store). |
| `path` | Required: a button without a menu path is `invalid`. |

- **Shown**: the icon; the tooltip is the command's shown title without a trailing "…" and its first active key ("Plugin Store (F9)"), plus the reason on a second line while the command is disabled or busy. Disabled or busy: drawn disabled, a click runs nothing. `checked: true`: the icon in the accent colour. Accessibility: a button named by the title, with its enabled and checked state and a default action.
- **Click**: runs the command exactly as a click on its menu item does.
- **Order and room**: left to right by `order`, the player's **Toggle Sidebar** rightmost; in a narrow window the strip loses cells from its outer (left) end inward: the lowest order goes first, the sidebar toggle last. `order` is position only: low is further left and goes first.
- **Limits** (Limits): one button per plugin (its first declared), eight in the player (the highest orders; the lowest go first, ties: the smaller plugin id, then the earlier declaration). A button past them is left out and logged with `limit`; the command and its menu entry stay.
- **Life cycle**: the button belongs to its command. Disposing the command, or disabling, stopping or uninstalling the plugin, removes it.
- **Older players** (before 0.5.10) build the declaration with their own copy of the SDK, which does not send `button`: the command and its menu entry work, without a button. Declare `"minPlayerVersion": "0.5.10"` when the button matters.

#### Binding syntax

```text
binding  = { modifier "+" } input      modifiers in the order Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Cmd, each at most once
input    = key name | one printable symbol | mouse input
```

- A letter is its key name in capitals, whatever the case typed: `Shift+E`.
- A symbol is written as typed and never with `Shift`: `">"`, not `"Shift+."`; `"!"`, not `"Shift+1"`. The `+` key is always `Plus`, also with modifiers (`Alt+Plus`).
- `"5"` is the main keyboard's 5 only, `"Numpad5"` the keypad's only; `"Enter"` is not the keypad's Enter (`"NumpadEnter"`). The menu shows keypad names as `Num5`, `Num+`, `NumEnter`.
- `Delete` is the forward-delete key ⌦ (fn+⌫ on a Mac laptop), `Backspace` is ⌫.
- On macOS `Ctrl` also matches ⌘ and `Cmd` only ⌘; on Windows `Cmd` is the Windows logo key. Write `Ctrl+…` for a binding that works on both.
- Mouse inputs apply over the video area only. The right button is not bindable (it opens the context menu).
- Anything else fails with code `invalid` when the command is added.

A menu item shows the first of its keyboard bindings that is in effect.

#### Binding names

| Field of `BINDING_INPUTS` | Names | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `modifiers` | `Ctrl`, `Alt`, `Shift`, `Cmd` | Modifiers, in the order a binding writes them. `Cmd` is ⌘ on macOS and the Windows logo key on Windows; on macOS `Ctrl` also matches ⌘. |
| `letters` | `A`–`Z` | Letter keys, by key name whatever the case: `A` to `Z`. |
| `digits` | `0`–`9` | Digit keys of the main keyboard: `0` to `9`. |
| `functionKeys` | `F1`–`F24` | Function keys: `F1` to `F24`. |
| `named` | `Space`, `Enter`, `Tab`, `Escape`, `Backspace`, `Delete`, `Insert`, `Home`, `End`, `PageUp`, `PageDown`, `ArrowLeft`, `ArrowRight`, `ArrowUp`, `ArrowDown`, `Plus`, `Numpad0`, `Numpad1`, `Numpad2`, `Numpad3`, `Numpad4`, `Numpad5`, `Numpad6`, `Numpad7`, `Numpad8`, `Numpad9`, `NumpadPlus`, `NumpadMinus`, `NumpadMultiply`, `NumpadDivide`, `NumpadEnter`, `NumpadDecimal` | Other named keys, matched by the physical key. `Plus` is the `+` key however it is typed; the `Numpad…` names are the numeric keypad only, never the main keyboard. |
| `mouse` | `Mouse:LeftClick`, `Mouse:LeftDoubleClick`, `Mouse:LeftDoubleClick:LeftHalf`, `Mouse:LeftDoubleClick:RightHalf`, `Mouse:MiddleClick`, `Mouse:X1`, `Mouse:X2`, `Mouse:WheelUp`, `Mouse:WheelDown`, `Mouse:WheelLeft`, `Mouse:WheelRight` | Mouse inputs on the video area. `:LeftHalf` and `:RightHalf` tell the halves of the video apart for a double click. |

#### Core actions

The player's own playback commands, which plugin.host.run runs by id (capability `commands`). Their bindings are stored as `host/<action>`; what each one does is on HostAction.

| Action | Menu item | Default bindings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stop` | Close | `F4` |
| `play-pause` | Playback ▸ Play/Pause | `Space`, `Mouse:LeftClick` |
| `previous` | Playback ▸ Previous | `PageUp`, `Mouse:X1` |
| `next` | Playback ▸ Next | `PageDown`, `Mouse:X2` |
| `frame-back` | Playback ▸ Seek ▸ Previous Frame | `D` |
| `frame-forward` | Playback ▸ Seek ▸ Next Frame | `F` |
| `seek-backward` | Playback ▸ Seek ▸ Back 5 s | `ArrowLeft` |
| `seek-forward` | Playback ▸ Seek ▸ Forward 5 s | `ArrowRight` |
| `rate-normal` | Playback ▸ Speed ▸ Normal | `Z` |
| `rate-down` | Playback ▸ Speed ▸ Slower 0.1 | `X` |
| `rate-up` | Playback ▸ Speed ▸ Faster 0.1 | `C` |
| `volume-up` | Audio ▸ Volume + | `ArrowUp`, `Mouse:WheelUp` |
| `volume-down` | Audio ▸ Volume − | `ArrowDown`, `Mouse:WheelDown` |
| `mute` | Audio ▸ Mute | `M` |
| `fullscreen` | Toggle Fullscreen | `Enter`, `Alt+Enter`, `F11` |

The player also owns **Toggle Fullscreen** (`host/fullscreen`), **Leave Fullscreen** (`host/exit-fullscreen`, `Escape`, only in fullscreen) and **Quit** (`host/quit`), and **Toggle Sidebar** (`host/sidebar`, player 0.5.10: the bottom bar's sidebar button, outside the menu, no default key); their keys are in Built-in commands.

#### Keys the system takes first

These keys may never reach a binding, because the system or the player takes them first; do not use them as defaults. This table is the one list of them; other pages link here.

| Keys | Taken by |
| --- | --- |
| ⌃F1–⌃F8 (macOS) | The system's keyboard navigation (⌃F1 turns keyboard access on and off). A `Ctrl+F1` binding still fires with ⌘F1. |
| ⌃← ⌃→ ⌃↑ ⌃↓ (macOS) | Spaces, Mission Control and application windows. The ⌘ versions of a `Ctrl+arrow` binding work. |
| ⌘H, ⌘M (macOS) | The system: hide and minimize the application. A `Ctrl+H` or `Ctrl+M` binding then fires only with ⌃. |
| ⌘Tab, ⌘Space (macOS) | The application switcher and Spotlight. |
| F11, and F1–F12 on Apple keyboards (macOS) | F11 shows the desktop; on Apple keyboards the function keys are media keys unless fn is held. |
| Ctrl+Alt+arrow keys (Windows) | Some graphics drivers, to rotate the screen. |
| Most `Cmd+…` combinations (Windows) | The system, for the Windows logo key. `Cmd+Q` (**Quit**) does nothing there; the window's close button and Alt+F4 quit. |
| **Standard close keys**: ⌘W (macOS); Ctrl+W, Ctrl+F4 (Windows) | The player, in a tool window, the floating sidebar and the Options window: they close that window exactly like the title-bar button (a tool window's `onClose` runs), even while a text field has focus, so neither Slint handlers nor bindings see them. In the main window they do nothing, so a binding for them fires there as usual. |
| Right button, left drag on the video | The player: the context menu; moving the window in window mode. |

The defaults of the built-in commands are taken as well: a plugin default on the same input in the same scope loses to the player's own command and to plugins loaded earlier.

## Reference: Platforms

A plugin uses the same API on macOS and Windows; the player does the system-specific part. This table lists everything that behaves differently. A call that a system cannot serve fails with `unsupported`, so a plugin handles that code instead of testing for the system (plugin.app.system() tells the system when a plugin must know).

| Feature | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clipboard | Text; PNG and JPEG images as their original bytes. | Text; images are converted to a bitmap and PNG. |
| Power.preventSleep | `caffeinate`. | The thread execution state. |
| Dialogs.confirm | An `NSAlert` sheet on the active player window (usually the tool window that asked), with the custom buttons and the checkbox. | A task dialog owned by the active player window, titled "Vestra Player", with the custom buttons; `destructive` shows a warning icon; a `checkbox` is asked as a second yes/no dialog after the user confirms. |
| MainWindow.setAlwaysOnTop | The floating window level. | Topmost window. |
| MainWindow.setVideoArea | The visible screen area, without the menu bar and the Dock. | The whole display. |
| MainWindow.setPictureInPicture | The system's picture-in-picture (macOS 14 or newer). | `unsupported`. |
| DropModifiers | The pointer and ⌥ ⇧ ⌘ (`cmd` is ⌘). | The pointer and Alt, Shift, Ctrl (`cmd` is Ctrl). |
| plugin.system (open, reveal) | Opened by the system; revealing several files selects all of them in one Finder window. | Opened by the shell; one Explorer window per folder. |
| plugin.secrets | The login keychain. | The Credential Manager. |
| App.system() | Version, build, model and displays; `rendering` is `"gpu"`, or `"software"` after a fallback (a window that cannot show GPU frames). | Version, build, model and displays; `rendering` is `"software"`. |
| Snapshots and exports (MediaCapture) | Available. | Available; needs FFmpeg 6.1 or newer. |
| Generated streams (Player.openStream) | A Unix socket. | Loopback TCP with a token. |
| Rendering | On the GPU (OpenGL), with hardware decoding. | In software, with hardware decoding copied back (`d3d11va-copy` and similar). |
| plugin.rendering (player 0.5.13) | `"gpu"` can be chosen unless the driver is ruled out (`denylist`, `previous-crash`). | `gpu.available` is `false` (`no-gpu-backend`); `setPreference("gpu")` fails with `unsupported`. |
| Render options (RenderOptions) | Available; `peakDetect` has no effect. | `unsupported` (software rendering). |
| Bindings | `Ctrl` also matches ⌘; `Cmd` is ⌘. | `Cmd` is the Windows logo key; `Cmd+Q` does not quit. |
| Keys taken first, standard close keys | See Keys the system takes first. | See Keys the system takes first. |
| Interface font | The system font; CJK falls back per character to the system's fonts (PingFang, Hiragino). | The system font; CJK falls back per character to Windows' CJK fonts in the interface language's order, then the bundled Noto Sans CJK SC (the chain). |
| `Theme.font-mono` | Menlo | Consolas |

Other systems have no released player; there, every feature in this table that needs the system fails with `unsupported` (always on top and `setVideoArea` with `unavailable`, `preventSleep` has no effect), and keys behave as on Windows.

When the player runs without a user interface (headless, as in some automated setups), opening windows, mounting panels, dialogs, the OSD and `settings.show` fail with `unavailable` on every system.

## Reference: Theme

What a plugin's Slint file can import from the player's library. How Slint and TypeScript talk is in Windows, panels, settings pages, dialogs and the OSD; which token to use where is in Guidelines: interface.

```slint nocheck
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";
import { Icon } from "@vestra/icons.slint";
import { Button, Slider, ToolTipArea, UrlInputRow } from "@vestra/widgets.slint";
import { MarkdownView, MarkdownBlocks, MarkdownBlock } from "@vestra/markdown.slint";
```

> **Current values; they may change — use the tokens.** The values below are what the player uses today. A later player may adjust them; a token keeps its meaning, a value you copy does not follow.

#### Colours

`Theme` colours follow the user's palette: `vestra`, the dark default, and `vestra-light` (player 0.4.0), whose video area stays dark. The player sets the palette on every view and again when the user switches, so read colours from `Theme` (they are read-only `out` properties) and never write a colour value yourself. The table shows both palettes' current values; the same values are THEME_PALETTES, for tests.

| `Theme.bg-video` | `#0a090e` | `#0e0d12` |  |
| `Theme.bg-list` | `#1a1821` | `#ffffff` |  |
| `Theme.bg-panel` | `#201d28` | `#f1eff5` |  |
| `Theme.line` | `#2b2734` | `#dcd8e4` |  |
| `Theme.hover-bg` | `#28232f` | `#e9e6f0` |  |

`std-widgets.slint` controls (`CheckBox`, `ComboBox`, `LineEdit`…) are compiled in Slint's `fluent-dark` style and switched to their light colours in `vestra-light`; do not set `Palette.color-scheme` yourself.

#### Sizes and fonts

Corner radii, font sizes and control sizes are constants, the same in both palettes. `radius-control` rounds controls, menu rows and hover plates; `radius-panel` menus, panels and the OSD (4px and 8px since player 0.4.0; 3px and 6px before).

| Token | Value | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Theme.radius-control` | `4px` |  |
| `Theme.radius-panel` | `8px` |  |
| `Theme.font-xs` | `9px` |  |
| `Theme.font-body` | `11px` |  |
| `Theme.font-tab` | `12px` |  |
| `Theme.font-title` | `13px` |  |
| `Theme.button-height` | `21px` |  |
| `Theme.button-min-width` | `66px` |  |
| `Theme.button-padding` | `8px` |  |
| `Theme.button-primary-height` | `24px` |  |
| `Theme.button-small-height` | `18px` |  |
| `Theme.button-small-min-width` | `41px` |  |
| `Theme.input-height` | `21px` |  |
| `Theme.checkbox-row-height` | `18px` |  |
| `Theme.label-height` | `14px` |  |
| `Theme.form-row-gap` | `26px` |  |
| `Theme.dialog-padding` | `14px` |  |

- **No font family of its own.** Every window uses the system's interface font for Latin text; a plugin does not need to set a font, and a `default-font-family` it sets stays first. A character the font lacks falls back, character by character, to a font for its script.
- **CJK fallback.** On macOS the system's own fallback (PingFang, Hiragino) covers Chinese, Japanese and Korean. On Windows the player sets a chain per script for every window, plugin windows included, and uses the first installed family that has the character:
  1. Windows' CJK families in the interface language's order: for Han text, the language's own tradition first (Simplified Chinese, the default for other languages: Microsoft YaHei UI, Microsoft YaHei, DengXian, SimSun, NSimSun, SimHei; Traditional Chinese: Microsoft JhengHei UI, Microsoft JhengHei, PMingLiU, MingLiU; Japanese: Yu Gothic UI, Meiryo UI, Yu Gothic, Meiryo, MS UI Gothic, MS Gothic; Korean: Malgun Gothic, Gulim, Dotum, Batang), then the other traditions. Kana starts with the Japanese families, Hangul with the Korean, Bopomofo with the Traditional Chinese.
  2. The family Windows' own fallback picks.
  3. The bundled Noto Sans CJK SC, last, so CJK text never shows as boxes when an edition lacks the optional font packs.
- **`Theme.font-mono`** is the system's monospace family: Menlo on macOS, Consolas on Windows (Platforms). CJK falls back in it too.

#### Icons

`@vestra/icons.slint` is the player's own icon set (player 0.4.0): round-capped, round-joined lines, 1.5px wide (1.25px for the small glyphs), never filled, each in its own box.

```slint nocheck
Icon { name: "play"; color: Theme.text; }                  // its box size
Icon { name: "close"; width: 20px; height: 20px; }         // scaled
```

- The box is the icon's default size; set `width` and `height` to scale it. An unknown name draws nothing.
- For a `Path` of your own, `Icons.commands(name)` returns the path data, `Icons.box-width(name)` and `Icons.box-height(name)` the box (the path's viewbox) and `Icons.line(name)` the line width.

#### Widgets

`@vestra/widgets.slint`: compact controls drawn with the theme. Other controls come from `std-widgets.slint`.

**`ToolTipArea`**: Hover for about half a second to show `text` beside the pointer. The tip closes when the pointer leaves, or presses on content that does not take the press itself; it shows again on the next hover. It is Slint's input-transparent tooltip: every press reaches the control under the pointer, and the tip does not take the keyboard focus. (Up to SDK 1.5.20 the tip was a PopupWindow, which swallowed the first press after it showed and took the focus while it was open.)

| Member | Kind | Default | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | in `string` |  |  |
| `showing` | out `bool` |  | The tip is showing (read-only); it follows the tip's delay closely, not exactly. |

**`Button`**: Dialog button: text (21px, or 18px when `small`), or an icon button when `text` is empty and `icon` holds Path data drawn in an icon-width × icon-height viewbox (filled, or 1.5px round-capped lines when `stroked`, as the @vestra/icons.slint set). The caller sizes icon buttons.

| Member | Kind | Default | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | in `string` |  |  |
| `icon` | in `string` |  |  |
| `icon-width` | in `length` | `14px` |  |
| `icon-height` | in `length` | `12px` |  |
| `stroked` | in `bool` |  |  |
| `enabled` | in `bool` | `true` |  |
| `small` | in `bool` |  |  |
| `checked` | in `bool` |  | Icon buttons: the "on" state, drawn in the accent colour. |
| `clicked` | callback `()` |  |  |

**`Slider`**: 2px line slider. Bar style (default): 8px round thumb, a white core in a 2px accent ring, gradient fill. Panel style (`panel: true`): 14×12 thumb, gradient fill. The track is `Theme.line` in both.

| Member | Kind | Default | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | in-out `float` |  |  |
| `minimum` | in `float` | `0` |  |
| `maximum` | in `float` | `1` |  |
| `enabled` | in `bool` | `true` |  |
| `panel` | in `bool` |  |  |
| `changed` | callback `(float)` |  |  |
| `released` | callback `(float)` |  |  |

**`UrlInputRow`**: Link input: a multi-line input and [Open] [Cancel]. Enter or the confirm button accepts (Shift+Enter starts a new line), Esc or Cancel cancels. No validation here: the plugin checks the address.

| Member | Kind | Default | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | in-out `string` |  |  |
| `placeholder` | in `string` |  |  |
| `confirm-text` | in `string` | `@tr("Open")` |  |
| `cancel-text` | in `string` | `@tr("Cancel")` |  |
| `enabled` | in `bool` | `true` |  |
| `accepted` | callback `(string)` |  |  |
| `cancelled` | callback `()` |  |  |
| `focus-input` | function `()` |  |  |
| `select-all` | function `()` |  |  |

A component's public functions are called from your own Slint code, through an element id: `row.focus-input()` puts the keyboard focus into `UrlInputRow`'s input (call it when the window opens, for example from `init`), `row.select-all()` selects its text.

#### Markdown

`@vestra/markdown.slint` shows a document made by plugin.ui.markdown: give `blocks` its value. Links report `link-clicked(url)`, resolved against the document's base; the plugin decides what to open (usually plugin.system). `code-copy: true` adds a Copy button to code blocks that reports `copy-code(code)`; the plugin copies it (plugin.clipboard).

**`MarkdownBlocks`**: Markdown blocks without scrolling, as tall as their content.

| Member | Kind | Default | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `blocks` | in `[MarkdownBlock]` |  |  |
| `code-copy` | in `bool` | `false` | A Copy button on code blocks, reporting `copy-code(code)`. |
| `link-clicked` | callback `(string)` |  |  |
| `copy-code` | callback `(string)` |  |  |

**`MarkdownView`**: A scrolling Markdown document.

| Member | Kind | Default | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `blocks` | in `[MarkdownBlock]` |  |  |
| `inset` | in `length` | `10px` | Space around the document. |
| `code-copy` | in `bool` | `false` | A Copy button on code blocks, reporting `copy-code(code)`. |
| `link-clicked` | callback `(string)` |  |  |
| `copy-code` | callback `(string)` |  |  |

Struct **`MarkdownRow`**: One table row (cells are plain text).

Struct **`MarkdownBlock`**: One displayed block. Plugins only pass these through; the fields are filled by the player.

#### Bar buttons

`@vestra/bar-buttons.slint` (player 0.5.10) is the strip of command buttons a bottom bar places at its right end: the buttons plugins give their commands (CommandOptions.button) and the player's sidebar toggle. The player fills and runs it; the bar only places it and gives it `room`, the width it can spare. See Writing a bottom bar.
