#### examples/signal-generator/main.ts

```ts
/**
 * Signal generator: Open ▸ Signal generator plays colour bars and a 1 kHz
 * sine tone that this plugin generates; choosing it again stops them.
 * Walkthrough: docs/examples/signal-generator.md.
 */
import type { Plugin, Stream, StreamFrame } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

export const WIDTH = 640;
export const HEIGHT = 360;
/** 29.97 fps, the NTSC frame rate: 48000 / FPS is not a whole number. */
export const FPS = 30000 / 1001;
/** Every stream's audio is 48 kHz stereo, 32-bit float. */
const SAMPLE_RATE = 48000;
const FREQUENCY = 1000; // Hz
const LEVEL = 0.25; // amplitude, −12 dBFS

/** Seven vertical 75 % colour bars as RGBA bytes, row by row from the top left. */
function colourBars(): Uint8Array {
  const colours: [number, number, number][] = [
    [191, 191, 191], // grey
    [191, 191, 0], // yellow
    [0, 191, 191], // cyan
    [0, 191, 0], // green
    [191, 0, 191], // magenta
    [191, 0, 0], // red
    [0, 0, 191], // blue
  ];
  const pixels = new Uint8Array(WIDTH * HEIGHT * 4);
  for (let y = 0; y < HEIGHT; y++) {
    for (let x = 0; x < WIDTH; x++) {
      const [r, g, b] = colours[Math.floor((x * 7) / WIDTH)]!;
      const i = (y * WIDTH + x) * 4; // the first byte of pixel (x, y)
      pixels[i] = r;
      pixels[i + 1] = g;
      pixels[i + 2] = b;
      pixels[i + 3] = 255; // alpha: opaque
    }
  }
  return pixels;
}

const video = colourBars(); // the picture never changes: draw it once
/** Room for the longest frame: 1602 stereo samples. */
const audio = new Float32Array(2 * Math.ceil(SAMPLE_RATE / FPS));
let owed = 0; // the fraction of a sample carried over to the next frame
let phase = 0; // position in the current sine cycle, 0 ≤ phase < 1

/** The `frame` callback of openStream: one picture and its audio. */
export function frame(): StreamFrame {
  // 48000 / 29.97 = 1601.6 samples: 1601 or 1602, never drifting.
  owed += SAMPLE_RATE / FPS;
  const samples = Math.floor(owed);
  owed -= samples;

  for (let i = 0; i < samples; i++) {
    const value = LEVEL * Math.sin(2 * Math.PI * phase);
    audio[2 * i] = value; // left
    audio[2 * i + 1] = value; // right
    phase += FREQUENCY / SAMPLE_RATE;
    if (phase >= 1) phase -= 1;
  }
  return { video, audio: audio.subarray(0, 2 * samples) };
}

export default function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  let stream: Stream | undefined; // the running stream
  let starting = false;

  async function start() {
    starting = true;
    try {
      stream = await plugin.player.openStream({
        width: WIDTH,
        height: HEIGHT,
        frame, // the player calls it whenever it needs the next frame
      });
      // Another source replaced the stream, or it failed.
      stream.onStop(() => (stream = undefined));
    } finally {
      starting = false;
    }
  }

  async function stop() {
    const running = stream;
    stream = undefined;
    await running?.stop();
  }

  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "signal-generator",
    path: ["@open", "Signal generator"], // the player's Open menu, in any language
    checked: () => stream !== undefined,
    run: () => {
      if (starting) return;
      return stream ? stop() : start();
    },
  });
}
```

#### examples/signal-generator/tests/signal-generator.test.ts

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin, TestHost } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate, { FPS, HEIGHT, WIDTH, frame } from "../main.ts";

test("a frame is RGBA colour bars and 1601 or 1602 stereo samples", () => {
  const { video } = frame();
  assert.equal(video.length, WIDTH * HEIGHT * 4);
  assert.deepEqual([...video.subarray(0, 4)], [191, 191, 191, 255]); // grey
  const last = video.length - 4; // bottom right: blue
  assert.deepEqual([...video.subarray(last)], [0, 0, 191, 255]);

  // 300 frames are 10.01 s: the audio stays within one sample of that.
  let total = 0;
  for (let n = 0; n < 300; n++) {
    const samples = frame().audio.length / 2;
    assert.ok(samples === 1601 || samples === 1602);
    total += samples;
  }
  assert.ok(Math.abs(total - (300 * 48000) / FPS) <= 1);
});

test("the sine continues smoothly from one frame to the next", () => {
  // The largest step a 1 kHz sine at amplitude 0.25 takes between samples.
  const maxStep = 0.25 * 2 * Math.PI * (1000 / 48000);
  let previous = frame().audio.at(-2)!; // the last left sample
  for (let n = 0; n < 10; n++) {
    const { audio } = frame();
    for (let i = 0; i < audio.length; i += 2) {
      assert.ok(Math.abs(audio[i]! - previous) <= maxStep + 1e-6);
      assert.equal(audio[i + 1], audio[i], "left = right");
      previous = audio[i]!;
    }
  }
});

/** Poll until `predicate()` holds: a stream starts and stops on timers. */
async function until(predicate: () => boolean) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + 3000;
  while (!predicate()) {
    if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error("timed out");
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 5));
  }
}

test("Open ▸ Signal generator starts the stream; choosing it again stops it", async () => {
  const host = new TestHost();
  // Windows has no Unix sockets: the frames travel over loopback TCP there.
  if (process.platform === "win32") host.producerTransport = "tcp";
  const { stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory: new URL("..", import.meta.url), // reads manifest.json
    host,
  });
  const command = () => host.command("signal-generator");
  try {
    const { declaration } = command();
    assert.deepEqual("path" in declaration && declaration.path, [
      "@open",
      "Signal generator",
    ]);

    await command().run();
    await until(() => command().state.checked === true);
    assert.equal(host.source.kind, "producer");

    await command().run();
    const producer = host.producers.get(1)!;
    await until(() => producer.released);
    assert.equal(producer.droppedWhileSelected, false, "source closed first");
    assert.equal(host.source.phase, "empty");
    assert.equal(command().state.checked, false);
  } finally {
    await stop();
  }
});
```

### Example: bookmark

A small, complete plugin: **Playback → Bookmark…** opens a tool window that remembers the current position and jumps back to it.

| Capabilities | API |
| --- | --- |
| `commands`, `ui.window`, `playback.read`, `events`, `playback.control` | `windows.create`, `Window.bind` / `on`, `player.state`, `player.seek` |

#### Walkthrough

A tool window whose buttons follow the playback state: **Mark** remembers where playback is, **Jump** goes back there. It shows the pattern most plugins with a window use: the window's properties are _bound_ to state, and its buttons call back into the plugin.

#### The manifest

(code: `manifest.json`, below)

| Capability         | Used for                                            |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `commands`         | the menu item                                       |
| `ui.window`        | the window                                          |
| `playback.read`    | reading the position and whether the video can seek |
| `events`           | keeping that state up to date while the plugin runs |
| `playback.control` | the seek                                            |

`minPlayerVersion` is 0.3.0 because the menu path uses the `@playback` menu id, which is new in that version.

#### The window

(code: `ui/bookmark.slint`, below)

- The buttons and layouts come from Slint's standard library.
- The file exports one component that inherits `Window`. `title` is the title bar's text.
- The three `in property` lines are the data the plugin writes: the label and whether each button is enabled.
- The two `callback` lines are what the window reports back: a click on each button.
- Each `Button` is enabled by one property and calls one callback.

Names are converted for you: Slint's `can-mark` is `canMark` in TypeScript.

#### The code

##### The state

(code: `main.ts`, part "state", below)

- `player` is `plugin.player`, kept in a constant because the code reads it several times.
- `mark` is the plugin's whole state: a position in seconds, or `null` for no bookmark.

##### The window, bound to the state

(code: `main.ts`, part "window", below)

- plugin.windows.create makes a handle. Nothing opens yet.
- window.bind gives the function that computes the window's properties. The SDK calls it again after every handler and every change of the player's state, and sends only what changed. So there is no update code:
  - `label` follows `mark`.
  - `canMark` follows `player.state.position`, which is `null` while nothing is open.
  - `canJump` needs a bookmark and a video that can seek.
- window.on handles a callback. `mark` stores the position; `jump` seeks back. The `!` is safe because the button is only enabled while there is a bookmark.
- Register callbacks before the first `show()`: a tool window takes its callbacks when it opens.

##### The menu command

(code: `main.ts`, part "command", below)

- `path: ["@playback", "Bookmark…"]` adds the item to the player's own **Playback** menu. A first segment that starts with `@` names a built-in menu (MenuId).
- `order: 270` places it among the Playback menu's items.
- `run` opens the window with window.show(). The bound values are already in place when it appears.

#### The test

(code: `tests/bookmark.test.ts`, below)

- `host.openElsewhere` and `host.setSource` play the user's part: a file is open at 42 seconds.
- `host.window("bookmark")` is the window, named after its file. `emit("mark")` acts like a click; `props` holds its properties by their Slint names.
- `await host.settle()` waits until the SDK has caught up. Settle before every assertion.
- After the jump, `host.source.position` is back at 42.

#### Try next

1. **Keep the bookmark after a restart** with plugin.storage`.json("bookmark", { defaults: { mark: null } })`. See Remember a window's state between runs.
2. **Show it on the seek bar** with a mark of kind `"bookmark"` from `plugin.timeline.layer()` (capability `timeline.marks`).
3. **A shortcut to jump**: a command with `title: "Jump to bookmark"`, `bindings: ["Ctrl+Alt+J"]` and `enabled: () => mark !== null`.

#### examples/bookmark/manifest.json

```json
{
  "id": "examples.bookmark",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "capabilities": [
    "commands",
    "ui.window",
    "playback.read",
    "events",
    "playback.control"
  ],
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.3.0"
}
```

#### examples/bookmark/main.ts

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

/**
 * Remembers the current playback position and jumps back to it: a command,
 * a tool window, and reading and changing the playback state.
 */
export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  const { player } = plugin;
  let mark: number | null = null;

  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/bookmark.slint");
  // Re-evaluated after every handler and player change; only changes are sent.
  window.bind(() => ({
    label: mark === null ? "No bookmark" : `Bookmark: ${mark.toFixed(1)} s`,
    canMark: player.state.position !== null,
    canJump: mark !== null && player.state.can.seek,
  }));
  // The Slint callbacks `mark` and `jump` of ui/bookmark.slint.
  window.on("mark", () => (mark = player.state.position));
  window.on("jump", () => player.seek(mark!));

  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "bookmark.open",
    path: ["@playback", "Bookmark…"],
    order: 270,
    run: () => window.show(), // opens it, or brings back the open one
  });
}
```

#### examples/bookmark/ui/bookmark.slint

```slint
import { Button, VerticalBox, HorizontalBox } from "std-widgets.slint";
export component BookmarkWindow inherits Window {
    title: "Bookmark";
    preferred-width: 320px;
    in property <string> label: "No bookmark";
    in property <bool> can-mark;
    in property <bool> can-jump;
    callback mark();
    callback jump();
    VerticalBox {
        Text { text: root.label; }
        HorizontalBox {
            Button { text: "Mark this position"; enabled: root.can-mark; clicked => { root.mark(); } }
            Button { text: "Jump to bookmark"; enabled: root.can-jump; clicked => { root.jump(); } }
        }
    }
}
```

#### examples/bookmark/tests/bookmark.test.ts

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin, TestHost } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

test("mark the position, then jump back to it", async () => {
  const host = new TestHost();
  host.openElsewhere("/movie.mp4");
  host.setSource({ duration: 600, position: 42 });
  const { stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory: new URL("..", import.meta.url),
    host,
  });

  await host.command("bookmark.open").run();
  const window = host.window("bookmark");
  window.emit("mark");
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(window.props.label, "Bookmark: 42.0 s");

  host.setSource({ position: 300 }); // playback moves on
  window.emit("jump");
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(host.source.position, 42);
  await stop();
});
```

### Example: panel-menu

A list in the player's sidebar with its own right-click menu. Next to the player's playlist it appears as a second sidebar tab, "Example list".

| Capabilities | API |
| --- | --- |
| `commands`, `ui.mount` | `panels.mount`, `Panel.bind` / `on`, `Panel.showMenu`, commands without a menu path |

#### Walkthrough

A list in the player's sidebar with its own right-click menu. It shows the two things that make a panel different from a tool window: its properties live on a Slint _global_, and its menu is made of the plugin's commands.

#### The manifest

(code: `manifest.json`, below)

`commands` for the two menu commands, `ui.mount` for the panel and its menu.

#### The list in Slint

(code: `ui/panel.slint`, below)

- `Theme` is the player's palette, supplied at run time as `@vestra/theme.slint`, so the list follows the player's colours.
- **The global `ListBridge`** holds the properties and callbacks. A panel is part of the player's main window, and the player makes a new instance of the component whenever it rebuilds that window. The global stays put, so the plugin talks to it, not to the component.
  - `rows` is the list (an array in TypeScript) and `selected` the selected index.
  - `select(int)` reports a click; `context-menu(float, float)` asks for the menu at a point.
- **The component** inherits `Rectangle`, not `Window`: the player places it. `for row[index] in ListBridge.rows` draws one 20-pixel row per item; the selected row gets `Theme.selected-bg`.
- **The `TouchArea`** of each row: any button going down selects the row. The right button coming up asks for the menu, at the pointer's position in the window (`absolute-position` is the row's position, `mouse-x`/`mouse-y` the pointer's position in it, and `/ 1px` makes a plain number).

#### The code

##### The state

(code: `main.ts`, part "state", below)

The list's titles and the selected index. Everything below reads and changes these two values.

##### Mounting the panel

(code: `main.ts`, part "mount", below)

- plugin.panels.mount puts the file's component in the `"sidebar"`. The SDK finds the component and the global by their `export` lines. `title` is used when the user detaches the sidebar into its own window.
- `bind` keeps the global's `rows` and `selected` equal to the state. The SDK re-runs it after every handler and command, and compares values, so an array changed in place (`splice`) is still sent.

##### The commands behind the menu

(code: `main.ts`, part "commands", below)

- Neither command has a `path`, so neither is in the main menu. A command without a path needs a `title`: the text in the right-click menu and in the shortcut settings.
- `enabled` greys **Remove** out when the list is empty.
- `remove` takes the item out and keeps `selected` inside the list.

##### The callbacks and the menu

(code: `main.ts`, part "menu", below)

- panel.on handles the global's callbacks. `contextMenu` is TypeScript's spelling of `context-menu`.
- panel.showMenu opens a menu of this plugin's commands at the point; `null` is a separator. Picking an item runs the command. Because the items are commands, they get disabled states and shortcut text for free.

#### The tests

(code: `tests/panel-menu.test.ts`, below)

- `host.mounted()` is the panel: `emit` fires a callback of the global, `props` holds its properties.
- `host.menus.at(-1)` is the last menu the plugin opened: the command ids, `null` for the separator, and the point.
- `host.command(id).run()` acts like picking the item in the menu.

#### Try next

1. **Keys that only work in the panel.** Add `focus: "panel"` and `bindings: ["Delete"]` to **Remove**: the key then works only while the list has focus, and keeps its usual meaning elsewhere.
2. **Next and previous.** Call plugin.player.provideSequence with `canNext`, `canPrevious`, `next` and `previous` that move `selected` (capabilities `playback.read`, `events`, `playback.control`): the player's own next/previous controls then step through the list.
3. **A check mark in the menu.** Add a command with `checked: () => …` and put it in the `showMenu` list.

#### examples/panel-menu/manifest.json

```json
{
  "id": "examples.panel-menu",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "ui.mount"]
}
```

#### examples/panel-menu/main.ts

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

/** A sidebar panel with its own right-click menu. */
export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  const items = ["First item", "Second item", "Third item"];
  let selected = 0;

  const panel = plugin.panels.mount("sidebar", "ui/panel.slint", {
    title: "Example list",
  });
  // Sent when the panel mounts, then whenever a value changes.
  panel.bind(() => ({ rows: items, selected }));

  const first = plugin.commands.add({
    id: "first",
    title: "Select the first item",
    run: () => (selected = 0),
  });
  const remove = plugin.commands.add({
    id: "remove",
    title: "Remove the selected item",
    enabled: () => items.length > 0,
    run: () => {
      items.splice(selected, 1);
      selected = Math.max(0, Math.min(selected, items.length - 1));
    },
  });

  // Callbacks of the bridge global; `bind` above sends the new selection.
  panel.on("select", (index: number) => (selected = index));
  // x and y: the pointer in window pixels, from the Slint file.
  panel.on("contextMenu", (x: number, y: number) =>
    panel.showMenu([first, null, remove], { x, y }),
  );
}
```

#### examples/panel-menu/ui/panel.slint

```slint
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";

export global ListBridge {
    in property <[string]> rows;
    in property <int> selected;
    callback select(int);
    callback context-menu(float, float);
}

export component ListPanel inherits Rectangle {
    background: Theme.bg-list;
    min-width: 200px;
    VerticalLayout {
        for row[index] in ListBridge.rows: Rectangle {
            height: 20px;
            background: index == ListBridge.selected ? Theme.selected-bg : transparent;
            Text {
                x: 6px;
                text: (index + 1) + ". " + row;
                color: index == ListBridge.selected ? Theme.text : Theme.text-list;
                font-size: Theme.font-body;
                vertical-alignment: center;
            }
            TouchArea {
                pointer-event(event) => {
                    if event.kind == PointerEventKind.down {
                        ListBridge.select(index);
                    }
                    if event.kind == PointerEventKind.up && event.button == PointerEventButton.right {
                        ListBridge.context-menu((self.absolute-position.x + self.mouse-x) / 1px,
                            (self.absolute-position.y + self.mouse-y) / 1px);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        // Takes the space below the rows. Without it the layout's maximum
        // height (three 20px rows) would cap the player's main window.
        Rectangle { vertical-stretch: 1; }
    }
}
```

#### examples/panel-menu/tests/panel-menu.test.ts

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

const directory = new URL("..", import.meta.url);

test("a right-click opens the panel's own menu", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, { directory });
  const panel = host.mounted();
  panel.emit("select", 2); // the right button goes down on the third row…
  panel.emit("context-menu", 40, 60); // …and comes up
  await host.settle();
  assert.deepEqual(host.menus.at(-1), {
    items: ["first", null, "remove"],
    x: 40,
    y: 60,
  });
  await stop();
});

test("the menu's commands change the list", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, { directory });
  const panel = host.mounted();
  panel.emit("select", 1);
  await host.command("remove").run();
  await host.settle();
  assert.deepEqual(panel.props.rows, ["First item", "Third item"]);
  assert.equal(panel.props.selected, 1);
  await host.command("first").run();
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(panel.props.selected, 0);
  await stop();
});
```

### Example: menus

An **Examples** menu with the speeds 0.5×, 1×, 1.5× and 2× as radio items, and below a separator a **Speed: 1×** item whose title changes when you pick a speed.

| Capabilities | API |
| --- | --- |
| `commands`, `playback.read`, `events`, `playback.control` | `commands.add` (`radio`, `checked`, `group`, `order`, `enabled`), `scope()`, `player.setRate` |

#### Walkthrough

What a menu item can look like: radio items, separator groups, a greyed-out item, and an item whose title changes. The items set the playback speed.

#### The manifest

(code: `manifest.json`, below)

`commands` for the menu items; `playback.read` and `events` to read the current speed and keep it up to date; `playback.control` to change it.

#### The code

##### Setup

(code: `main.ts`, part "setup", below)

`player` is `plugin.player`, kept in a constant because the code reads it several times.

##### An item whose title changes

(code: `main.ts`, part "title", below)

A command's title and path cannot change after it is added. To change them, remove the command and add it again; a child scope makes that easy.

- `status` is a child scope from plugin.scope(). Everything added through it belongs to it.
- `showSpeed` disposes the old scope, which removes the old item from the menu, then makes a new scope and adds the item with the new title.
- `order: 860` puts it after the speeds; `group: "status"` differs from the speeds' group, so the player draws a separator line between them.
- `enabled: false` greys it out: it only shows information. `run` is still required.
- The last line adds the first version, with the current speed.

##### Radio items

(code: `main.ts`, part "radio", below)

- The loop adds one command per speed. `entries()` gives the index for `order`, so the items appear in that order (850 to 853).
- All four share the menu path's first segment, `"Examples"`, so they land in the same submenu; the submenu itself sits where its first item sits.
- `group: "speeds"` keeps them in one block.
- `radio: true` draws `checked` as a dot instead of a check mark. Which item is checked is the plugin's decision: `checked` compares the player's current speed with this item's. The SDK re-evaluates it whenever the player's state changes, so the dot also moves when the speed changes in some other way.
- `enabled` greys the items out while the video cannot change speed, for example with nothing open.
- `run` changes the speed with player.setRate, then rebuilds the status item.

#### The tests

(code: `tests/menus.test.ts`, below)

- `host.openElsewhere` opens a file, so the speed can change.
- `host.command(id).declaration` is the command as declared (`radio`, `group`, `path`); `state` is what the player shows now (`checked`, `enabled`).
- After `rate-1.5` runs, the `speed` command has been declared again with the new title.

#### Try next

1. **Keep the title in step** when the speed changes elsewhere: call `showSpeed` from `plugin.player.onChange` when `state.rate` differs from the last value shown.
2. **A check item.** Add a command with `checked: () => player.state.paused` (no `radio`) that toggles pause.
3. **A repeating key.** Give a command `bindings: ["Ctrl+Alt+ArrowUp"]` and `repeat: true`: it runs again while the key is held, which suits small steps such as volume.

#### examples/menus/manifest.json

```json
{
  "id": "examples.menus",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "playback.read", "events", "playback.control"]
}
```

#### examples/menus/main.ts

```ts
import type { Plugin, Scope } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

/** Menu items: radio items, separator groups and a title that changes. */
export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  const { player } = plugin;

  let status: Scope = plugin.scope();
  async function showSpeed(rate: number) {
    await status.dispose(); // removes the previous item from the menu
    status = plugin.scope();
    status.commands.add({
      id: "speed",
      path: ["Examples", `Speed: ${rate}×`],
      order: 860,
      group: "status",
      enabled: false,
      run() {},
    });
  }
  await showSpeed(player.state.rate);

  for (const [index, rate] of [0.5, 1, 1.5, 2].entries())
    plugin.commands.add({
      id: `rate-${rate}`,
      path: ["Examples", `${rate}×`],
      order: 850 + index,
      group: "speeds",
      radio: true,
      checked: () => player.state.rate === rate,
      enabled: () => player.state.can.rate,
      run: async () => {
        await player.setRate(rate);
        await showSpeed(rate);
      },
    });
}
```

#### examples/menus/tests/menus.test.ts

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin, TestHost } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

const directory = new URL("..", import.meta.url);

test("the speeds are radio items in their own group", async () => {
  const host = new TestHost();
  host.openElsewhere("/movie.mp4"); // a file is open, so the speed can change
  const { stop } = await startPlugin(activate, { directory, host });
  const half = host.command("rate-0.5").declaration;
  assert.ok("radio" in half && half.radio);
  assert.equal(half.group, "speeds");
  assert.equal(host.command("rate-1").state.checked, true);

  await host.command("rate-2").run();
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(host.command("rate-2").state.checked, true);
  assert.equal(host.command("rate-1").state.checked, false);
  await stop();
});

test("the status item is added again with a new title", async () => {
  const host = new TestHost();
  host.openElsewhere("/movie.mp4");
  const { stop } = await startPlugin(activate, { directory, host });
  assert.deepEqual(host.command("speed").declaration.path, [
    "Examples",
    "Speed: 1×",
  ]);
  await host.command("rate-1.5").run();
  await host.settle();
  assert.deepEqual(host.command("speed").declaration.path, [
    "Examples",
    "Speed: 1.5×",
  ]);
  await stop();
});
```

### Example: theme-widgets

**Examples → Theme widgets…** opens a tool window drawn with the player's own theme and widgets (`@vestra/theme.slint`, `@vestra/widgets.slint`): two sliders, a small button, icon buttons and tooltips.

| Capabilities | API |
| --- | --- |
| `commands`, `ui.window` | `windows.create`, `Window.bind` / `on`; `Theme`, `Button`, `Slider`, `ToolTipArea` in Slint |

#### Walkthrough

A tool window drawn with the player's own theme and controls, so it looks like part of the player: its colours, spacing, buttons, sliders and tooltips.

#### The manifest

(code: `manifest.json`, below)

`commands` for the menu item, `ui.window` for the window.

#### The window

(code: `ui/theme-widgets.slint`, below)

From top to bottom:

- **The imports.** `@vestra/theme.slint` and `@vestra/widgets.slint` are supplied by the player at run time. `Theme` holds the palette, fonts and sizes; `Button`, `Slider` and `ToolTipArea` look like the player's own controls. For editor support, point the Slint language server's library path `vestra` at `node_modules/@vestra-player/sdk/slint/vestra`.
- **The window.** A fixed `width`; `Theme.bg-panel` instead of a hard-coded colour, so the background follows the player's palette.
- **The properties.** `level` is `in-out` because both the plugin and the user change it; `label` is only written by the plugin. `level-changed` reports a drag; `reset` reports the reset buttons.
- **The layout.** `Theme.dialog-padding` and `Theme.font-body` give the spacing and text size of the player's dialogs.
- **`ToolTipArea`** shows its `text` after the pointer rests on its content for about half a second (600 ms before player 0.5.2). The tip never takes a press or the keyboard focus: a click goes to the control under the pointer even while the tip shows.
- **The sliders** are bound _two-way_ to `level` with `<=>`, so dragging one moves the other at once, inside Slint. `changed` passes the value to the plugin. A one-way binding (`value: root.level`) would be broken by Slint the first time the user moved the slider. `panel: true` is the panel style; without it, the bar style.
- **`Button`** with `text` is a dialog button; `small: true` is the 18-pixel one.
- **Icon buttons** have no `text`; `icon` is SVG-style path data drawn in an `icon-width` × `icon-height` box (14×12 by default). `stroked: true` draws lines instead of filling. `checked` draws the icon in the accent colour.

#### The code

##### The window and its state

(code: `main.ts`, part "window", below)

- `level` is the plugin's state, 0 to 1.
- bind keeps the window's `level` and `label` equal to it.
- `levelChanged` stores the dragged value. `bind` then sends it back, but it is the value the slider already shows, so nothing jumps.
- `reset` sets the state back to 0.5; `bind` moves both sliders and the label.

##### The menu command

(code: `main.ts`, part "command", below)

`run` opens the window, or brings it back if it is hidden.

#### The test

(code: `tests/theme-widgets.test.ts`, below)

`emit` plays the user's part (a drag, a click on **Default**); `props` shows what the window displays afterwards.

#### Try next

1. **Use the level.** Add `ui.osd` and show the level with `plugin.osd.show` when the slider is released (the `Slider`'s `released` callback).
2. **A text field.** Add `UrlInputRow` from `@vestra/widgets.slint`, the player's input row with confirm and cancel buttons.
3. **More tokens.** The concept page lists every `Theme` token and widget property.

#### examples/theme-widgets/manifest.json

```json
{
  "id": "examples.theme-widgets",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "ui.window"]
}
```

#### examples/theme-widgets/main.ts

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

/** A tool window drawn with the player's own theme and widgets. */
export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  let level = 0.5;
  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/theme-widgets.slint");
  window.bind(() => ({ level, label: `Level ${Math.round(level * 100)}` }));
  window.on("levelChanged", (value: number) => (level = value));
  window.on("reset", () => (level = 0.5));

  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "open",
    path: ["Examples", "Theme widgets…"],
    run: () => window.show(),
  });
}
```

#### examples/theme-widgets/ui/theme-widgets.slint

```slint
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";
import { Button, Slider, ToolTipArea } from "@vestra/widgets.slint";

export component ThemeWidgets inherits Window {
    title: "Theme widgets";
    width: 301px;
    background: Theme.bg-panel;
    in-out property <float> level;
    in property <string> label;
    callback level-changed(float);
    callback reset();
    VerticalLayout {
        padding: Theme.dialog-padding;
        spacing: 12px;
        HorizontalLayout {
            spacing: 8px;
            ToolTipArea {
                text: "Drag a slider, or press Default";
                width: 65px;
                Text { text: root.label; color: Theme.text; font-size: Theme.font-body; horizontal-alignment: right; vertical-alignment: center; }
            }
            Slider { panel: true; value <=> root.level; changed(value) => { root.level-changed(value); } }
            Button { text: "Default"; small: true; clicked => { root.reset(); } }
        }
        Slider { value <=> root.level; changed(value) => { root.level-changed(value); } }
        HorizontalLayout {
            alignment: end;
            spacing: 8px;
            ToolTipArea {
                text: "Reset";
                Button { width: 25px; icon: "M 3 2.5 L 11 10.5 M 11 2.5 L 3 10.5"; stroked: true; clicked => { root.reset(); } }
            }
            Button { width: 25px; icon: "M 0 0 L 12 6 L 0 12 Z"; icon-width: 12px; checked: root.level > 0.5; }
        }
    }
}
```

#### examples/theme-widgets/tests/theme-widgets.test.ts

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

test("the sliders report the level; Default resets it", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory: new URL("..", import.meta.url),
  });
  await host.command("open").run();
  const window = host.window("theme-widgets");
  assert.equal(window.props.label, "Level 50");

  window.emit("level-changed", 0.8); // the user drags a slider
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(window.props.label, "Level 80");

  window.emit("reset"); // the user presses Default
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(window.props.level, 0.5);
  assert.equal(window.props.label, "Level 50");
  await stop();
});
```

### Example: markdown

**Examples → Markdown example…** opens a window that shows `sample.md` with the player's `MarkdownView` component: headings, lists, code, quotes, a table and an image from the package. The manifest also has the display fields the plugin manager shows (`name`, `author`, `punchline`, `description`, `tags`, `icon`, `license`).

| Capabilities | API |
| --- | --- |
| `commands`, `ui.window` | `ui.markdown`, `MarkdownView` from `@vestra/markdown.slint`, `Window.set`; package assets in `package.json` (`"vestra": { "assets": [...] }`) |

#### Walkthrough

A window that shows a formatted Markdown document with the player's `MarkdownView` component. The plugin never parses Markdown: it passes the text to the player, which parses and draws it.

#### The manifest

(code: `manifest.json`, below)

- `commands` for the menu item, `ui.window` for the window. `plugin.ui.markdown` needs no capability.
- `minPlayerVersion: "0.2.0"`: `ui.markdown` is new in that version, and older players refuse the plugin with a clear message.
- `name` to `license` are display fields for the plugin manager. They do not affect how the plugin runs, and any plugin can have them; Manifest lists their rules.

#### The package file

(code: `package.json`, below)

`vestra-plugin build` leaves Markdown files out of the package (except `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and the manifest's `readme` and `changelog`; see What build puts into dist/), so `sample.md` is listed under `"vestra": { "assets": [...] }`, which copies files into the package as they are. `assets/icon.png` needs no entry: the build copies images anyway.

#### The window

(code: `ui/document.slint`, below)

- `MarkdownView` and its block type `MarkdownBlock` come from `@vestra/markdown.slint`, supplied by the player at run time.
- The preferred and minimum sizes give the window its first size and keep it usable when shrunk.
- `doc` is the document, a `[MarkdownBlock]` property. The plugin never builds these blocks itself; it writes the value `plugin.ui.markdown` returns.
- `MarkdownView` fills the window and scrolls a long document.

#### The code

##### Imports

(code: `main.ts`, part "imports", below)

`readFileSync` reads the document; `fileURLToPath` turns the module's address into a path.

##### The window and the command

(code: `main.ts`, part "document", below)

- `directory` is the folder `main.ts` (or, in a package, `main.js`) is in: the package directory, wherever it is installed.
- plugin.windows.create makes the window handle; nothing opens yet.
- `run` does three things each time the item is chosen:
  1. It reads `sample.md` from the package. Reading it on every run means an edited file shows its changes the next time.
  2. plugin.ui.markdown prepares the document. `base` is what relative images resolve against, so `assets/icon.png` in the text means the package's icon. Without `base`, the image shows its alternative text.
  3. window.set writes the document, then `show()` opens the window. `set` rather than `bind`, because the document is a one-off value, not something computed from state. Set before `show()`, it is there when the window appears.

#### The test

(code: `tests/markdown.test.ts`, below)

host.markdown() reads the document back from the window's property: its `text` and its `base`.

#### Try next

1. **Open links.** Add `callback open-link(string);` to the window, forward `link-clicked(url) => { root.open-link(url); }` from `MarkdownView`, and handle it with `window.on("openLink", (url: string) => plugin.system.openUrl(url))` before the first `show()`.
2. **Remote images.** Put `![Avatar](https://github.com/vestrasys.png?size=128)` in the document: `ui.markdown` downloads `https:` images first (pass `remoteImages: false` to turn that off).
3. **Copy code.** Set `code-copy: true` on `MarkdownView`: code blocks get a **Copy** button (labelled in the interface language) that reports `copy-code(code)`. Forward it as a callback and copy the text with plugin.clipboard, which needs the `clipboard` capability.
4. **Show the plugin's own README** instead of `sample.md`; the build always packs the README.

#### examples/markdown/manifest.json

```json
{
  "id": "examples.markdown",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "ui.window"],
  "name": "Markdown example",
  "author": "Vestra Player",
  "punchline": "A window that shows a Markdown document",
  "description": "Opens a window that shows a Markdown document: headings, lists, code, quotes, tables and an image.",
  "tags": ["Example", "Markdown"],
  "icon": "assets/icon.png",
  "license": "Apache-2.0",
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.2.0"
}
```

#### examples/markdown/main.ts

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

/** A tool window that shows a Markdown document. */
export default async function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  // Relative links and images in sample.md resolve against this folder.
  const directory = fileURLToPath(new URL(".", import.meta.url));
  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/document.slint");
  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "show",
    path: ["Examples", "Markdown example…"],
    run: async () => {
      const text = readFileSync(new URL("sample.md", import.meta.url), "utf8");
      // `doc` is the window's [MarkdownBlock] property, drawn by MarkdownView.
      window.set({ doc: await plugin.ui.markdown(text, { base: directory }) });
      await window.show();
    },
  });
}
```

#### examples/markdown/sample.md

````md
# Markdown example

This window shows the **core Markdown component**: *italic*, ~~strikethrough~~ and `inline code`.

## Lists

- A bulleted list
- A second item, with **bold** text
  1. A nested numbered list
  2. Its second item
- [x] A finished task
- [ ] An open task

## Code and quotes

```ts
const doc = await plugin.ui.markdown(text, { base });
window.set({ doc });
```

> The player parses and draws the Markdown; the plugin only passes the text.

## Tables

| Element | Supported |
| --- | --- |
| Headings, paragraphs, lists | Yes |
| Code blocks, quotes, tables | Yes |
| Inline HTML | No (not shown) |

## Images

A local image, `assets/icon.png` in the package, found through `base`:

![Icon](assets/icon.png)
````

#### examples/markdown/ui/document.slint

```slint
import { MarkdownView, MarkdownBlock } from "@vestra/markdown.slint";
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";

export component Document inherits Window {
    title: "Markdown example";
    preferred-width: 520px;
    preferred-height: 560px;
    min-width: 280px;
    min-height: 200px;
    background: Theme.bg-panel;
    in property <[MarkdownBlock]> doc;
    MarkdownView {
        blocks: root.doc;
    }
}
```

#### examples/markdown/tests/markdown.test.ts

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

const directory = new URL("..", import.meta.url);

test("the window shows sample.md, with the package as its base", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, { directory });
  await host.command("show").run();
  await host.settle();
  const window = host.window("document");
  assert.equal(window.visible, true);
  const doc = host.markdown(window.props.doc);
  assert.ok(doc);
  assert.match(doc.text, /^# Markdown example/);
  assert.equal(doc.base, fileURLToPath(directory));
  await stop();
});
```

### Example: i18n

A plugin in the player's language: **Tools → Counter…** opens a window with one button that counts clicks. Every text is English in the source; `locales/zh-Hans.po` translates it into Simplified Chinese, and the player shows the translation when its interface language is Simplified Chinese.

| Capabilities | API |
| --- | --- |
| `commands`, `ui.window`, `ui.osd` | `commands.add`, `windows.create`, `osd.show(template, args)`; Slint `@tr`; `vestra-plugin i18n extract` and `check`; tests with `startPlugin({ locale })` |

#### Walkthrough

A plugin in the player's language. **Tools ▸ Counter…** opens a window with one button; each click counts and shows the count on the video. All texts are English in the source, and `locales/zh-Hans.po` translates them: with the player in Simplified Chinese the menu reads **工具 ▸ 计数器…** and the window **2 次点击**. The plugin contains no translation code.

#### The code

(code: `main.ts`, below)

- The menu path is English. The player shows each segment translated with the plugin's catalog; menus of all plugins merge by these English words.
- The window gets data (`count`), not text.
- plugin.osd.show takes a template and its arguments. The player translates `"Count: {}"`, then puts `count` into `{}`. A sentence built in TypeScript (`` `Count: ${count}` ``) could not be translated.

#### The window

(code: `ui/counter.slint`, below)

Every text is in `@tr("…")`. The player replaces the English literal with the translation when it loads the file; Slint then fills in the arguments. `"{n} click" | "{n} clicks" % root.count` has two forms: the first for 1, the second for every other number (`{n}` is the number).

#### The translation

`vestra-plugin i18n extract` collected the texts into `locales/messages.pot`; `extract --locale zh-Hans` started `locales/zh-Hans.po`, and each `msgstr` was then filled in:

(code: `locales/zh-Hans.po`, below)

Chinese has one plural form, so `msgstr[0]` is enough. `vestra-plugin i18n check` reports what is missing; `vestra-plugin build` compiles the file into `dist/locales/zh-Hans.json`, which the player reads.

#### The test

(code: `tests/main.test.ts`, below)

`startPlugin(activate, { directory, locale })` loads the catalog of that language. `host.command(id).display` is the menu as the user sees it, `declaration` what the code declared; `host.osd` lists the messages as shown.

#### examples/i18n/manifest.json

```json
{
  "id": "examples.i18n",
  "version": "0.1.0",
  "apiVersion": "vestra/1",
  "entry": "main.ts",
  "minPlayerVersion": "0.4.3",
  "capabilities": ["commands", "ui.window", "ui.osd"],
  "name": "Counter",
  "author": "Vestra Player SDK examples",
  "punchline": "A click counter in the player's language",
  "description": "Tools ▸ Counter… opens a window with one button that counts clicks.\nSDK example: a plugin translated into Simplified Chinese.",
  "tags": ["example"]
}
```

#### examples/i18n/main.ts

```ts
/**
 * Counter: Tools ▸ Counter… opens a window with one button that counts
 * clicks, in the player's language. The texts are English; the player
 * translates them with locales/<lang>.po. Walkthrough: docs/examples/i18n.md.
 */
import type { Plugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk";

export default function activate(plugin: Plugin) {
  let count = 0;

  // The window's texts are in its Slint file (@tr); TypeScript passes data.
  const window = plugin.windows.create("ui/counter.slint");
  window.bind(() => ({ count }));
  window.on("add", () => {
    count += 1;
    // A template and its arguments, never a sentence built in TypeScript.
    return plugin.osd.show("Count: {}", [count]);
  });

  // Declared texts are English; the player shows them translated.
  plugin.commands.add({
    id: "counter",
    path: ["Tools", "Counter…"],
    run: () => window.show(),
  });
}
```

#### examples/i18n/ui/counter.slint

```slint
// The Counter window. Every text is @tr("English"): the player puts the
// translation in its place when it loads the file. Walkthrough:
// docs/examples/i18n.md.
import { Theme } from "@vestra/theme.slint";
import { Button } from "@vestra/widgets.slint";

export component CounterWindow inherits Window {
    title: @tr("Counter");
    width: 240px;
    background: Theme.bg-panel;

    in property <int> count;
    callback add();

    VerticalLayout {
        padding: Theme.dialog-padding;
        spacing: 8px;
        Text {
            // One form for 1, the other for every other number.
            text: @tr("{n} click" | "{n} clicks" % root.count);
            color: Theme.text;
            font-size: Theme.font-body;
        }
        Button {
            text: @tr("Add one");
            clicked => { root.add(); }
        }
    }
}
```

#### examples/i18n/tests/main.test.ts

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";
import { startPlugin } from "@vestra-player/sdk/testing";
import activate from "../main.ts";

const directory = new URL("..", import.meta.url); // manifest.json and locales/

test("English: the texts as written", async () => {
  const { host, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory,
    locale: "en",
  });
  const counter = host.command("counter");
  assert.deepEqual(counter.display.path, ["Tools", "Counter…"]);
  await counter.run();
  host.window("counter").emit("add");
  await host.settle();
  assert.deepEqual(host.osd, ["Count: 1"]);
  await stop();
});

test("Simplified Chinese: the menu and the message from locales/zh-Hans.po", async () => {
  const { host, plugin, stop } = await startPlugin(activate, {
    directory,
    locale: "zh-Hans",
  });
  assert.equal(plugin.i18n.locale, "zh-Hans");
  const counter = host.command("counter");
  // The key stays English; the menu shows the translation.
  assert.deepEqual(counter.declaration.path, ["Tools", "Counter…"]);
  assert.deepEqual(counter.display.path, ["工具", "计数器…"]);
  await counter.run();
  const window = host.window("counter");
  window.emit("add");
  window.emit("add");
  await host.settle();
  assert.equal(window.props["count"], 2);
  assert.deepEqual(host.osd, ["计数：1", "计数：2"]);
  await stop();
});
```
